s: The First Backward Classes Commission was appointed in which year, and its report was submitted in which year?
x: The First Backward Classes Commission was appointed in 1953 and submitted its report in 1955. It was headed by Kaka Kalelkar.

s: Which government implemented the Mandal Commission recommendations in 1990?
x: The V.P. Singh Government implemented the Mandal recommendations in 1990; 27 per cent of Central civil posts were reserved for OBCs from 1993.

s: Which commission is associated with recommending reservation for backward classes in government employment, leading to the 27 per cent OBC quota?
x: The B.P. Mandal Commission (1979) is the commission on reservation in government employment (APPSC 2019, GS 2019); it recommended 27 per cent for OBCs. Kalelkar's report (1955) was not implemented; Rohini deals with OBC sub-categorisation; R.N. Prasad framed creamy-layer criteria.

s: What was the main objective of the Oversight Committee headed by M. Veerappa Moily in 2006?
o: To prepare the Central List of Scheduled Tribes
To implement OBC reservation by expanding seats so that general-category seats did not shrink
To identify the creamy layer among SCs and STs
To abolish reservation in Central educational institutions
x: The Oversight Committee headed by M. Veerappa Moily planned implementation through expansion of seats, thereby protecting the existing number of general-category seats.

s: For what purpose was the Justice G. Rohini Commission constituted in 2017?
o: identifying the first list of OBCs under Article 340
determining the constitutional validity of EWS reservation
preparing the list of Scheduled Tribes
x: The Justice G. Rohini Commission was constituted in 2017 to examine the sub-categorisation of OBCs.

s: Which of the following findings was associated with the Justice G. Rohini Commission?
o: About 97% of OBC benefits were taken by 25% of the sub-castes, while about 1,000 communities had zero representation.
The Commission found that only 100 Central-list OBC communities required sub-categorisation.
About 25% of benefits went to 97% of the sub-castes, while no community lacked representation.
All Central-list OBC castes received an equal share of benefits.
x: The Commission found that approximately 97% of benefits had been taken by 25% of the sub-castes, while around 1,000 communities had zero representation.

s: Into how many sub-groups did the Justice G. Rohini Commission propose to divide the Central-list OBCs?
x: The proposal associated with the Commission envisaged three to four sub-groups among the Central-list OBCs.

s: Which requests does the National Commission for Backward Classes mainly examine?
o: Appointment of judges to the Supreme Court
Inclusion in or exclusion from backward-class lists
x: The NCBC examines requests for inclusion in or exclusion from the lists of backward classes and advises on such matters.

s: Which commission was the first to use social and educational criteria for identifying backward classes?
x: The Kaka Kalelkar Commission was the first to use social and educational tests to identify backward classes.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Justice G. Rohini Commission?
o: It examined sub-categorisation within OBCs in the Central List
It examined sub-categorisation of Scheduled Tribes in the Central List
It aimed at equitable distribution of reservation benefits among under-represented groups
It submitted its report to the President on 31 July 2023
x: The Rohini Commission examined sub-categorisation of OBCs, not Scheduled Tribes, in the Central List so that benefits reach under-represented groups.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Justice G. Rohini Commission – Sub-categorisation within the OBC Central List
B.P. Mandal Commission – Foundation for the PESA Act, 1996
Kaka Kalelkar Commission – 27% reservation for OBCs
Bhuria Committee – First Backward Classes Commission
x: The Rohini Commission studied OBC sub-categorisation; Kalelkar was the First Backward Classes Commission, Mandal recommended 27% for OBCs and Bhuria laid the basis for PESA.

s: How many backward castes were identified by the B.P. Mandal Commission?
x: The Mandal Commission identified 3,743 backward castes. The other options shuffle the same digits.

s: What did the Kaka Kalelkar Commission recommend?
o: Sub-categorisation within the Central OBC List
27% reservation for OBCs based on 11 indicators
x: Kalelkar recommended a caste-based census and reservations; sub-categorisation was Rohini's task, 27% and 11 indicators Mandal's, and 15% for minorities Ranganath Misra's.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the B.P. Mandal Commission?
o: It was the second Backward Classes Commission.
It was constituted by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.
x: The Mandal Commission was set up through the Ministry of Home Affairs, not Social Justice and Empowerment; it identified 3,743 backward castes and recommended 27% for OBCs.

s: On whose report were the OBC creamy-layer criteria in the DoPT Office Memorandum of September 1993 based?
x: The creamy-layer criteria were framed through the DoPT Office Memorandum of September 1993, based on the Justice R.N. Prasad Expert Committee.

s: The Mandal Commission (1979) was set up through which Ministry?
o: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
x: The Janata Government of Morarji Desai set up the Mandal Commission through the Ministry of Home Affairs; the Rohini Commission came through Social Justice and Empowerment.

s: How many backward castes were identified by the Kaka Kalelkar Commission?
x: The Kalelkar Commission listed 2,399 backward castes, 837 of them 'most backward'; 3,743 is the Mandal figure.

s:
Consider the following statements about the B.P. Mandal Commission:
1. It used 11 indicators of backwardness.
2. It estimated OBCs at 52 per cent of the population.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: the Mandal Commission used 11 social, educational and economic indicators and put the OBC share at 52 per cent.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Kaka Kalelkar Commission:
1. It was the first commission to use social and educational criteria for backwardness.
2. Its recommendations were implemented by the Central Government.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Only 1 is correct: the Kalelkar Commission first used social and educational criteria, but its report was not implemented and was rejected in 1961.

s: On which date did the Justice G. Rohini Commission submit its report to the President?
x: The Rohini Commission, set up in October 2017, reported on 31 July 2023; 30 March 1955 was the Kalelkar report.

s: Who was the Chairman of the First Backward Classes Commission appointed in 1953?
x: The First Backward Classes Commission (1953-55) was headed by Kaka Kalelkar; the Second (1979) was headed by B.P. Mandal.

s: Who headed the commission set up in October 2017 to examine sub-categorisation of OBCs?
x: The Justice G. Rohini Commission (2017) examined sub-categorisation of the Central-list OBCs and reported in July 2023.

s: Which Prime Minister's government set up the Second Backward Classes Commission in 1979?
x: The Mandal Commission was set up in 1979 by the Janata Government of Morarji Desai; V.P. Singh implemented it in 1990.

s: During whose tenure as Prime Minister was the First Backward Classes Commission appointed in 1953?
x: The Kaka Kalelkar Commission was appointed by the President on 29 January 1953, when Nehru's government was in office.

s: Which commission recommended 15 per cent reservation for minorities?
x: The Ranganath Misra Commission recommended a 15 per cent quota for minorities.

s: Who was appointed Chairperson of the National Commission for Backward Classes in 2026?
x: Niranjan Jyoti was appointed NCBC chairperson in 2026; the NCBC became constitutional under Article 338B by the 102nd Amendment.

s: Under which Act was the National Commission for Backward Classes first set up as a statutory body?
o: National Commission for Backward Classes Act, 1993
Central Educational Institutions (Reservation in Admission) Act, 2006
Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
x: The NCBC was statutory under the NCBC Act, 1993 (repealed in 2018) before the 102nd Amendment made it constitutional.

s: Which clause was added to the Constitution to overcome the judgment in State of Madras v. Champakam Dorairajan?
x: Article 15(4) was inserted by the First Amendment, 1951 to overcome Champakam Dorairajan. Article 16(4) was in the original Constitution; Article 15(5) came by the 93rd Amendment (2005) and Article 16(4B) by the 81st (2000).

s: With which of the following is the 76th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1994 associated?
o: Inserting Article 16(4A) for reservation in promotion
Placing Tamil Nadu's 69 per cent reservation law in the Ninth Schedule
Giving constitutional status to the NCBC
x: The 76th Amendment (1994) placed Tamil Nadu's 69 per cent reservation law in the Ninth Schedule. Article 16(4A) came through the 77th (1995), consequential seniority through the 85th (2001), and constitutional status of the NCBC through the 102nd (2018).

s: Which amendment-clause pair is correctly matched?
x: The First Amendment, 1951 inserted Article 15(4). Article 16(4A) was inserted by the 77th Amendment, Article 16(4B) by the 81st, Article 15(5) by the 93rd and Article 16(6) by the 103rd Amendment.

s: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct?
o: The 82nd Amendment concerns relaxation of qualifying standards in promotion for SCs and STs.
The 81st Amendment deals with unfilled backlog vacancies.
The 89th Amendment introduced the relaxation of qualifying marks under Article 335.
The 77th Amendment deals with reservation in promotion for SCs and STs.
x: The 89th Amendment did not introduce the relaxation of qualifying marks; that change was made by the 82nd Amendment Act, 2000. The 89th Amendment is associated with the bifurcation of the SC/ST Commission.

s: Which of the following Constitutional Amendment–provision pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: 77th Amendment – Reservation in promotion under Article 16(4A)
81st Amendment – Backlog vacancies as a separate class
x: The 82nd Amendment inserted the proviso to Article 335 on relaxing qualifying marks; consequential seniority came with the 85th.

s: Which Constitutional Amendment restored the power of the States to identify and list SEBCs?
x: The 105th Amendment Act, 2021 restored the States' power to list SEBCs; the 102nd (2018) had given the NCBC constitutional status and inserted Article 342A.

s: With which of the following is the 85th Constitutional Amendment (2001) associated?
x: The 85th Amendment gave consequential seniority with promotion, nullifying the 'catch-up' rule; backlog carry-forward was the 81st and relaxed marks the 82nd.

s:
Consider the following statements about constitutional amendments on reservation:
1. The 82nd Amendment provided relaxed qualifying marks in promotion for SCs/STs.
2. The 89th Amendment inserted Article 16(4B) on backlog vacancies.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Only 1 is correct: the 82nd Amendment added the proviso to Article 335; the 89th split the SC/ST Commission, and 16(4B) came from the 81st.

s: Under which Bill number was the 105th Constitutional Amendment Act introduced in Parliament?
x: The 105th Amendment was the 127th Bill; the 102nd was the 123rd Bill and the 103rd the 124th Bill.

s: The 103rd Constitutional Amendment Act on EWS reservation was introduced as which Constitution Amendment Bill?
x: The 103rd Amendment (10% EWS quota) came from the 124th Bill, 2019; the 102nd came from the 123rd Bill and the 105th from the 127th Bill.

s: The 102nd Constitutional Amendment Act, which gave constitutional status to the NCBC, was introduced as which Bill?
x: The 102nd Amendment (Article 338B, 342A) was the 123rd Bill; the 103rd was the 124th and the 105th was the 127th.

s: Under which Article of the Constitution was the Mandal Commission appointed?
x: Article 340 lets the President appoint a commission on the conditions of SEBCs; the Constitution does not define 'backward classes'.

s: According to the Indra Sawhney judgment, on what basis are the backward classes under Article 16(4) mainly identified?
x: Indra Sawhney held that backward classes under Article 16(4) are identified mainly by caste and social backwardness, not by economic criteria alone.

s: In the term SEBC used in Article 342A, what does the letter 'E' stand for?
x: SEBC means Socially and Educationally Backward Classes; 'Economically' is the usual distractor.

s: Under Article 340, who appoints a commission to investigate the conditions of backward classes?
x: Article 340 empowers the President to appoint a commission on socially and educationally backward classes; Kalelkar, Mandal and Rohini were set up under it.

s: For the Central Educational Institutions Act, OBCs are the classes 'so determined' by whom?
x: Under the CEI (Reservation in Admission) Act, OBCs are the classes so determined by the Central Government.

s: Where is the expression 'Backward Classes' defined in the Constitution?
x: The Constitution does not define 'Backward Classes'; Article 340 only provides for a commission to investigate their conditions.

s: Before the 102nd Amendment, Article 338(10) said references to Scheduled Castes would include such backward classes as were specified by whom?
x: Before the 102nd Amendment, Article 338(10) treated references to Scheduled Castes as including such backward classes as the President specified. Consequently, complaints relating to backward classes could go to the SC Commission.

s: Article 15(5) was inserted by which Constitutional Amendment Act?
x: The 93rd Amendment (2005) inserted Article 15(5), enabling reservation in educational institutions including private unaided ones, but excluding minority institutions.

s: What does Article 16(4B) of the Constitution provide for?
o: Reservation in promotion for SCs and STs
Carrying forward unfilled backlog vacancies as a separate class
10 per cent EWS reservation in posts
x: Article 16(4B), added by the 81st Amendment (2000), treats unfilled backlog vacancies as a separate class outside the 50 per cent ceiling.

s: Which of the following reservation provisions was part of the original Constitution?
x: Article 16(4) was in the original Constitution; 15(4) came by the 1st (1951), 16(4A) by the 77th and 15(5) by the 93rd Amendment.

s: Under which Article of the Constitution is the National Commission for Backward Classes a constitutional body?
x: The 102nd Amendment (2018) inserted Article 338B, giving the NCBC constitutional status; 338A is the NCST and 342A deals with SEBC lists.

s: Which Article of the Constitution, inserted by the 102nd Amendment, deals with the lists of Socially and Educationally Backward Classes?
x: Article 342A, added by the 102nd Amendment (2018), deals with SEBC lists; 338B is the NCBC.

s:
Match the following:
List-I (Article)
A. 338B
B. 342A
C. 366(26C)
D. 340
List-II (Content)
1. Commission to investigate backward classes
2. Definition of SEBCs
3. National Commission for Backward Classes
4. SEBC lists
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: 338B is the NCBC, 342A the SEBC lists, 366(26C) defines SEBCs and 340 provides for a backward classes commission.

s: Which educational institutions are kept outside reservation in admissions under Article 15(5)?
x: Article 15(5), added by the 93rd Amendment, covers private aided and unaided institutions but excludes minority institutions.

s:
Consider the following statements about Article 15(5):
1. It allows reservation in admission to private unaided educational institutions.
2. It applies to minority educational institutions.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Article 15(5) covers private aided and unaided institutions, but minority institutions are excluded.

s: Indra Sawhney directed a permanent statutory body for backward-class lists. Which body did it later become?
x: The permanent statutory body directed for backward-class lists subsequently became the National Commission for Backward Classes.

s: What did the Indra Sawhney judgment hold about carry-forward of unfilled reserved vacancies?
o: Unlimited and calculated once in a decade
Allowed, within the 50 per cent ceiling applied year by year
x: Indra Sawhney permitted carry-forward of vacancies, subject to the 50 per cent ceiling being applied year by year.

s: The 93rd Constitutional Amendment (2005), which inserted Article 15(5) enabling reservation in admissions including private institutions, was enacted to overcome which judgment?
x: Article 15(5) was inserted by the 93rd Amendment to overcome P.A. Inamdar (2005), which had barred quotas in private unaided institutions; it excludes minority institutions and is the basis of the CEI Act, 2006. Indra Sawhney concerns Mandal, M. Nagaraj promotion reservation, Janhit Abhiyan EWS.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Indra Sawhney judgment?
o: Caste may be the main criterion for backwardness.
OBC reservation was extended to promotions as a general rule.
The creamy layer among OBCs should be excluded.
Total reservation should ordinarily not exceed 50 per cent.
x: Indra Sawhney confined reservation to initial appointments, not promotions.

s: Which case held that reservation should generally stay within 50 per cent and that caste is not the sole test?
o: State of Madras v. Champakam Dorairajan
M.R. Balaji v. State of Mysore
x: M.R. Balaji (1962) laid down the 50 per cent limit and held caste is not the sole test of backwardness.

s: Which case upheld the 93rd Amendment and the 27 per cent OBC quota under the CEI Act?
x: Ashoka Kumar Thakur (2008) upheld the 93rd Amendment and the 27 per cent OBC quota, applying the creamy layer to OBCs but not SCs/STs.

s: What did the Supreme Court decide in the Maratha reservation case (Jaishri Patil, 2021)?
o: Upheld the Maratha quota as an extraordinary case
Struck down the Maratha SEBC quota as breaching the 50 per cent limit
x: Jaishri Patil (5 May 2021) struck down the Maratha quota, finding no extraordinary case beyond 50 per cent; its ruling on SEBC lists was reversed by the 105th Amendment.

s: Which of the following case–ruling pairs is correctly matched?
o: Jarnail Singh – creamy layer can apply to SC/ST promotions
M. Nagaraj – struck down the 77th Amendment
P.A. Inamdar – upheld quota in private unaided institutions
Champakam Dorairajan – upheld a caste-based quota
x: Jarnail Singh (2018) allowed the creamy layer in SC/ST promotions; Nagaraj upheld the 77th, Inamdar barred quota in private unaided institutions, and Champakam struck the quota down.

s: On which point did Indra Sawhney overrule M.R. Balaji?
o: Reservation must stay within 50 per cent
Caste can be the main criterion of backwardness
Creamy layer must be excluded from SCs
x: Indra Sawhney held caste can be the main criterion of backwardness, overruling Balaji on this; it kept the 50 per cent ceiling and denied promotion quota.

s: Which case held that a promotion quota for SCs and STs needs data on backwardness, inadequacy of representation and efficiency?
x: In M. Nagaraj (2006) the Supreme Court upheld the 77th, 81st, 82nd and 85th Amendments but required such data before a promotion quota.

s: In which case did the Supreme Court hold in March 2026 that parental salary alone cannot place a candidate in the OBC creamy layer?
o: Union of India v. Rohith Nathan
x: In Union of India v. Rohith Nathan (11 March 2026) the Court held parental salary alone cannot decide creamy-layer status and ordered supernumerary posts.

s: In which year did the CEI (Reservation in Admission) Act, 2006, giving 27 per cent OBC reservation, come into force?
x: Although enacted in 2006, the Central Educational Institutions (Reservation in Admission) Act came into force in 2007.

s: In which year did the 27 per cent OBC quota in Central Government jobs begin?
x: The Mandal recommendations were implemented in 1990, but the 27 per cent quota in central posts operated from 1993; the CEI Act seats came in 2007.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched in relation to the Andhra Pradesh BC groups?
o: BC-E — aboriginal tribes and nomadic groups
x: BC-D consists of other classes. BC-B comprises vocational or occupational groups, BC-C comprises SC converts to Christianity, and BC-E comprises socially and educationally backward Muslims.

s: What is the combined quota share of the BC-A to BC-E groups in Andhra Pradesh?
x: The shares are 7 per cent, 10 per cent, 1 per cent, 7 per cent and 4 per cent respectively, totalling 29 per cent.

s: What was the effect of the Supreme Court’s interim order concerning the 4 per cent reservation for backward Muslim groups in Andhra Pradesh?
o: It permanently approved the quota without further judicial examination.
It allowed the quota to continue pending consideration by a Constitution Bench.
It converted the quota into an EWS reservation.
It abolished the quota immediately after the High Court judgment.
x: Although the Andhra Pradesh High Court struck down the 2007 Act in 2010, the Supreme Court permitted the 4 per cent quota to continue by an interim order pending a Constitution Bench.

s: What was the outcome of the Sukhdev case on backward-class reservation in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Caste alone could not be the basis, and 112 classes were identified using poverty, residence and occupation.
All reservation for backward classes was unconstitutional.
Caste alone could be the basis for identifying backward classes.
Reservation could be based only on residence.
x: The High Court held in the Sukhdev case that caste alone could not be the basis; consequently, 112 classes were listed using poverty, residence and occupation as considerations.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Kapu reservation proposal?
o: The Justice Manjunatha Commission was constituted in 2016.
In 2019, Kapus got 5% within the EWS quota, later withdrawn.
A 2017 Bill proposed 5% reservation for Kapus as BC-F.
The Centre approved the 2017 BC-F proposal.
x: The Centre never approved the 2017 BC-F proposal.

s:
Assertion (A): BC reservation in Andhra Pradesh local bodies was reduced to 24.15 per cent under GOs 176, 559 and 560.
Reason (R): N.T. Rama Rao introduced a 20 per cent BC quota in local bodies in 1984.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
x: Both are correct, but the 1984 introduction of the quota does not explain its later reduction from 34 to 24.15 per cent.

s: The BC-E category in Andhra Pradesh was added through which measure and in which year?
x: BC-E was added by the Andhra Pradesh Act of 2007. Earlier lists commonly included only BC-A to BC-D.

s: Which commission was the first Andhra Pradesh Backward Classes Commission and framed the A-D grouping along with a 25 per cent quota?
x: The Anantharaman Commission was the first Andhra Pradesh Backward Classes Commission; its report was submitted in 1970 and it framed the A-D grouping and a 25 per cent quota.

s: Which of the following is NOT part of the Supreme Court's triple test for OBC reservation in local bodies?
o: Prior approval of the quota by the National Commission for Backward Classes
A dedicated commission to examine backwardness
Determination of the reservation proportion local-body-wise
Keeping total reservation within the 50 per cent ceiling
x: The triple test is a dedicated commission, local-body-wise proportion and a total within 50 per cent; NCBC approval is not one of its parts.

s: What was the BC quota in AP local bodies when N.T. Rama Rao introduced it in 1984?
x: NTR introduced a 20 per cent BC quota in 1984; it was later raised to 34 per cent and cut to 24.15 per cent under GOs 176, 559 and 560.

s: Under which category did the Justice Manjunatha Commission (2016) propose a 5 per cent quota for Kapus?
x: The Manjunatha Commission led to a 2017 Bill giving Kapus 5 per cent as BC-F; it was never approved by the Centre.

s: What is the reservation quota for the BC-E group (socially and educationally backward Muslims) in Andhra Pradesh?
x: The BC-E group, added by the 2007 Act, has a 4 per cent quota within the 29 per cent BC total in Andhra Pradesh.

s:
Consider the following statements about Muslim reservation in Andhra Pradesh:
1. The 5 per cent Muslim quota of 2004 was struck down by the AP High Court.
2. The 4 per cent quota under the 2007 Act was struck down by the AP High Court in 2010.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The 5% quota (2004, 2005) and the 2007 Act's 4% quota were both struck down by the AP High Court; a Supreme Court interim order lets the 4% continue.

s: Which Andhra Pradesh commission, which took charge in January 1982, reviewed BC reservation and the inclusion of minorities?
x: The Muralidhara Rao Commission took charge on 27 January 1982 and reviewed BC reservation in AP.

s: Under which Articles was EWS reservation, which stands outside the 50 per cent ceiling, provided?
x: The 50 per cent ceiling applies to backward-class reservations; EWS reservation was added over and above it through Articles 15(6) and 16(6).

s: To which institutions does EWS reservation in admissions under the 103rd Amendment extend?
x: EWS reservation applies to Central educational institutions and posts and extends to private educational institutions; it is not mandatory for the States.

s: The Union Government opposed the creamy layer for SCs and STs because their status flows from which Articles?
x: In August 2026, the Union Government opposed the proposal, stating that SC/ST status flows from Articles 341 and 342.

s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the categories associated with the OBC creamy layer under the Indra Sawhney framework?
o: All children of persons belonging to OBC communities, irrespective of social or economic status
Children whose parents are both Class-II officers
x: The framework identifies specified socially advanced categories, including children of Class-I officers and parents who are both Class-II officers. It does not exclude all OBC children irrespective of their circumstances.

s: What is the present income ceiling for the OBC creamy layer, fixed in the 2017 revision?
x: The income ceiling was revised to ₹8 lakh per annum in 2017 and is stated to remain current.

s: What was the OBC creamy-layer income limit when it was first fixed in 1993?
x: The limit was Rs 1 lakh in 1993, raised to Rs 2.5 lakh (2004), Rs 4.5 lakh (2008), Rs 6 lakh (2013) and Rs 8 lakh (2017).

s: In which year was the OBC creamy-layer income limit raised to Rs 6 lakh a year?
x: The limit went from Rs 1 lakh (1993) to 2.5 lakh (2004), 4.5 lakh (2008), 6 lakh (2013) and 8 lakh (2017).

s: What is the nature of EWS reservation under the 103rd Amendment for the States?
o: Mandatory only for State educational institutions
Mandatory only for State government posts
x: The amendment enables up to 10% EWS reservation outside SC/ST/OBC quotas but does not make it mandatory for States.

s: For EWS eligibility, below what size must the family's agricultural land be?
x: The EWS criteria are family income below Rs 8 lakh, agricultural land below 5 acres and a flat below 1,000 sq ft.

s: By what majority was the 103rd Constitutional Amendment upheld in Janhit Abhiyan v. Union of India?
x: The EWS amendment was upheld 3:2, with Chief Justice U.U. Lalit and Justice S. Ravindra Bhat dissenting.

s: Which Chief Justice dissented on EWS reservation in Janhit Abhiyan (2022)?
x: The five-judge bench upheld EWS by 3:2; the dissenters were CJI U.U. Lalit and Justice S. Ravindra Bhat.

s: For which economically weaker sections is EWS reservation under the 103rd Amendment meant?
o: Not covered by SC, ST or OBC quotas
Including OBCs above the creamy layer only
Within the existing SC and ST quotas
x: The 10 per cent EWS quota is for sections not covered by SC/ST/OBC quotas and is over and above existing reservation.

s:
Consider the following statements about EWS eligibility under the 103rd Amendment:
1. Family income must be below Rs 8 lakh a year.
2. The family should not own a flat of 1,000 sq ft or more.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: EWS criteria are family income below Rs 8 lakh, agricultural land below 5 acres and a flat below 1,000 sq ft.

s: Why did the Forest Conservation Rules, 2022 become a subject of dispute between the NCST and the Environment Ministry?
o: Added a compulsory tribal veto over every forest diversion
Dropped the forest-dwellers’ consent clause before forest diversion
Prohibited all development projects in forest areas
Transferred all forests to Gram Sabhas
x: The 2022 Rules dropped the consent clause of forest-dwellers before forest diversion, leading to a dispute between the NCST and the Environment Ministry.

s: Which is the nodal Ministry for implementing the Forest Rights Act, 2006?
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
x: The Ministry of Tribal Affairs is the nodal ministry for the Forest Rights Act, 2006.

s: Under the Forest Rights Act, each Sub-Divisional and District Level Committee has how many members?
x: The Sub-Divisional and District Level Committees are six-member bodies of revenue, tribal and forest officials and elected panchayat members.

s: Which of the following is NOT recognised as a forest right under the Forest Rights Act, 2006?
o: Automatic ownership of all mineral resources beneath forest land
Habitat rights for Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups
x: The Act recognises rights such as minor forest produce, community forest resource management and PVTG habitat rights. It does not confer automatic ownership of all mineral resources beneath forest land.

s: The Forest Rights Act, 2006 sought to undo the historical injustice done to whom?
x: The Act recognises forest rights of Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers, with the stated objective of undoing historical injustice to forest dwellers.

s: A forest-dwelling Scheduled Tribe family claims recognition of rights under the Forest Rights Act. Which date is relevant for determining occupation of forest land?
x: Forest-dwelling Scheduled Tribes must have been occupying the forest land before 13 December 2005 for eligibility under the stated cut-off criterion.

s: For how long must Other Traditional Forest Dwellers show residence in or dependence on forests for recognition under the Forest Rights Act?
x: Other Traditional Forest Dwellers must show residence in or dependence on forests for three generations, specified as 75 years, before 2005.

s: What is the maximum extent of forest rights that may be recognised per family under the Forest Rights Act, 2006?
x: The ceiling for forest rights is up to four hectares per family.

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with an individual forest right rather than a community forest right?
x: Habitation and self-cultivation are individual rights. Nistar, grazing, fishing and community forest resource management are examples of community rights.

s: What is the position of the Forest Rights Act, 2006 in relation to laws inconsistent with it?
o: Applies only where no State law exists
Can be overridden by an executive circular
x: The Forest Rights Act overrides laws that are inconsistent with its provisions.

s: Which Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group was the first to receive habitat rights under the Forest Rights Act?
x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (Baiga of Madhya Pradesh); it is added as option 5.
The first habitat rights in India went to the Baiga of Baigachak (Dindori, Madhya Pradesh) in 2015-16; the Bharia of Patalkot (MP) got them only in 2022 and the Baiga and Kamar of Chhattisgarh later, so the old key 'Bharia' was wrong and no printed option is correct.

s: Under the Forest Rights Act, 2006, what type of right is 'nistar'?
x: Nistar, grazing, fishing and ownership and disposal of minor forest produce are listed community rights under the FRA.

s: What is to be done with areas of national parks and sanctuaries declared Critical Wildlife Habitat under the Forest Rights Act?
o: Transferred exclusively to private conservation agencies
Kept inviolate after an open process involving affected communities
Opened for mining after approval by the Forest Department
x: Critical Wildlife Habitats are areas within national parks and sanctuaries to be kept inviolate, and they are notified after an open process with affected communities.

s: The Indian Forest (Amendment) Act, 2017 did which of the following?
o: Removed bamboo grown outside forest areas from the definition of “tree”.
Granted an unrestricted right to fell bamboo in forest areas.
Removed all bamboo from the definition of minor forest produce.
Transferred ownership of all bamboo to private companies.
x: The 2017 amendment removed bamboo grown outside forest areas from the definition of “tree”. It did not confer a right to fell bamboo in forest areas.

s: Which one of the following statements regarding bamboo under the Forest Rights Act is correct?
o: Bamboo is a tree in every location and cannot be collected by forest dwellers.
Bamboo is a minor forest produce, and ownership is vested in forest dwellers.
Bamboo is excluded from minor forest produce and belongs only to the Forest Department.
Ownership of bamboo is vested only in Gram Panchayats.
x: The Forest Rights Act treats bamboo as a minor forest produce and vests its ownership in forest dwellers.

s: Which of the following is NOT a reported gap in Forest Rights Act implementation?
o: Excessive focus on individual titles over CFR
Strong MoTA capacity ensuring complete CFR implementation
x: The identified gap is weak, not strong, MoTA capacity; the other three are reported implementation gaps.

s: What is the status of Social Impact Assessment under the RFCTLARR Act, 2013?
o: Required only for private projects and never for public projects
Replaced by a census of affected families
x: The RFCTLARR Act, 2013 makes Social Impact Assessment mandatory.

s: In Scheduled Areas, acquisition under the RFCTLARR Act is treated as a last resort and requires consent of which body or bodies?
o: Only the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes
Gram Sabha, Panchayat or Autonomous Council, as applicable
x: Acquisition in Scheduled Areas is a last resort and requires consent from the Gram Sabha, Panchayat or Autonomous Council, as applicable.

s: In August 2026, which Ministry stated that the Forest Rights Act has no provision for Gram Sabha consent for Stage-II forest clearance?
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
x: The Ministry of Tribal Affairs stated in August 2026 that the FRA has no provision for Gram Sabha consent for Stage-II forest clearance.

s: From which Ministry did the Ministry of Tribal Affairs seek funds for managing Community Forest Resource areas vested in Gram Sabhas?
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
x: MoTA sought MoEFCC funds for managing CFR areas vested in Gram Sabhas; this is separate from the criticism of the Agasthyamalai evictions.

s: Besides forest-dwelling Scheduled Tribes, whose forest rights does the Forest Rights Act, 2006 recognise?
x: The Act recognises individual and community forest rights of forest-dwelling STs and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers.

s: Which of the following pairs relating to the Forest Rights Act is correctly matched?
o: Rights vested – Individual and community forest rights
x: The FRA was passed in 2006, came into force on 31 December 2007, had its rules notified on 1 January 2008, and vests individual and community forest rights.

s: What was the outcome of the Niyamgiri bauxite-mining proposal in 2013?
o: It was approved after the Forest Rights Act process was waived.
It was approved after consent from the State legislature.
Dongria Kondh Gram Sabhas rejected the mining under the FRA, and the project was cancelled.
It was transferred to private pumped-storage projects.
x: In 2013, Dongria Kondh Gram Sabhas rejected bauxite mining under the Forest Rights Act, after which the project was cancelled.

s: Under the RFCTLARR Act, 2013, the consent requirement is what percentage of affected families for private projects and public-private partnership projects, respectively?
x: Consent of 80% of affected families is required for private projects and 70% for PPP projects.

s: On which date did the Forest Rights Act, 2006 come into force?
x: The Act came into force on 31 December 2007 and its rules on 1 January 2008; 13 December 2005 is the cut-off date.

s: Under the Forest Rights Act, how many titles have been distributed in Andhra Pradesh?
x: AP has distributed 2,26,651 titles covering 4,54,706 acres.

s: Under the Forest Rights Act, what type of right is ownership of minor forest produce?
x: Ownership of minor forest produce, like nistar, grazing and CFR management, is a community right under FRA; bamboo counts as MFP.

s: The Forest (Conservation) Amendment Act, 2023 exempts strategic projects located within what distance of the borders?
x: The 2023 Amendment exempts strategic projects within 100 km of the borders, a point in the tribal rights debate.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Forest Rights Act, 2006?
o: The Gram Sabha initiates determination of rights
Its nodal ministry is Tribal Affairs
It gives ownership of minerals to forest dwellers
The ceiling is 4 ha per family
x: The Act gives no ownership of minerals; the Gram Sabha initiates claims, Tribal Affairs is the nodal ministry and the ceiling is 4 ha.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct regarding forest diversion and the Forest Rights Act?
o: MoEF's 2009 circular required completion of FRA processes before forest diversion under the FCA
Under the 2009 circular, forest diversion could go ahead before FRA claims were settled if the project was of public importance
Gram Sabha consent is relevant to the FRA process
Niyamgiri saw Gram Sabha rejection of bauxite mining
x: MoEF's August 2009 circular barred forest diversion under the FCA until FRA processes, including Gram Sabha consent, were complete; it made no public-importance exception. In Niyamgiri (2013) the Gram Sabhas rejected bauxite mining. The Forest Conservation Rules, 2022 later diluted this sequencing.

s: In scheduling a community as a Scheduled Tribe, which body first examines the State's proposal?
x: The sequence is State proposal, Registrar General of India, NCST, Union Cabinet, and amendment by Parliament under Article 342(2).

s: The term 'Scheduled Tribes' is defined in which provision of the Constitution of India?
x: Article 366(25) defines Scheduled Tribes. Article 342(2) lets Parliament modify the ST list, Article 338A creates the NCST, and Article 244(1) applies the Fifth Schedule to Scheduled Areas.

s: For what is the Lokur Committee (1965) known?
o: Laying down five criteria for identifying Scheduled Tribes
Studying the health and educational status of tribes in 2013
x: The Lokur Committee gave five ST criteria; Bhuria was the basis of PESA, Dhebar studied Scheduled Areas and Xaxa reported in 2013.

s: Which of the following is NOT one of the Lokur Committee criteria for Scheduled Tribes?
x: The five criteria are primitive traits, distinct culture, geographical isolation, shyness of contact and backwardness; ST status is religiously neutral.

s: Under which Article was the Dhebar Commission (1960-61) on Scheduled Areas and ST welfare set up?
x: The U.N. Dhebar Commission was set up under Article 339; Article 340 is for backward classes and 342 for ST lists.

s: Which of the following committee–work pairs is correctly matched?
o: Lokur Committee – Article 339 Commission on Scheduled Areas
Xaxa Committee – five ST criteria of 1965
Dhebar Commission – 2013 study of tribal health and education
x: The Bhuria Committee formed the basis of PESA; Dhebar was the Article 339 Commission, Lokur gave the 1965 criteria and Xaxa did the 2013 study.

s: Who headed the High-Level Committee (2013) on the socio-economic, health and educational status of tribes?
x: Virginius Xaxa headed the 2013 High-Level Committee; Dhebar headed the 1960-61 Commission and Bhuria the committee behind PESA.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Scheduled Tribe status does not depend on the religion a person follows.
2. Parliament can amend the Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950 under Article 342(2).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: ST status is religiously neutral, unlike SC status, and Article 342(2) lets Parliament change the ST list.

s: Which Article of the Constitution provides for the Fifth Schedule on the administration of Scheduled Areas?
x: Article 244(1) applies the Fifth Schedule to Scheduled Areas; 338A is the NCST, 342 the ST lists and 366(25) defines STs.

s: Which Constitutional Amendment created the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes under Article 338A?
x: Article 338A was inserted by the 89th Constitutional Amendment, 2003; NCST functions from 19 February 2004 with civil-court powers.

s: Up to what annual income does NSTFDC lend to Scheduled Tribes?
x: NSTFDC, set up in 2001, lends to STs with income up to double the poverty line, not three times.

s: Raising farm output with improved seeds and fertilisers, planting fruit trees and other income-raising work in tribal areas are objectives of which programme?
x: Agricultural improvement, fruit-bearing plantations and other income-generating activities in tribal areas are objectives of TADP/ITDA.

s: When did monitoring of the Tribal Sub-Plan move from the Planning Commission to the Ministry of Tribal Affairs?
x: TSP monitoring shifted to MoTA in January 2017; online monitoring now covers the ST component of 41 ministries.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: TRIFED — 1987 — tribal marketing and MSP for Minor Forest Produce
Roshni — 2018 — residential schools for SC students
VDVKs — 2013 — skills and jobs in LWE districts
PM Janjatiya Vikas Mission — 1987 — sanitation mechanisation
x: TRIFED was established in 1987 and is associated with tribal marketing and MSP for Minor Forest Produce. The other options interchange the purposes or years of different programmes.

s: Which body purchases minor forest produce at fair prices, runs PDS depots and gives credit to tribal farmers in Andhra Pradesh?
x: The Girijan Cooperative Corporation (GCC) purchases MFP at fair prices, runs PDS depots and provides credit to tribal farmers.

s: Which body implements the NAMASTE scheme?
x: NAMASTE, associated with MoSJE and MoHUA, is implemented by NSKFDC with an allocation of Rs 349.70 crore; TRIFED is not its implementing agency.

s: In which Five Year Plan was the Tribal Sub-Plan first adopted?
x: The Tribal Sub-Plan was first adopted in the Fifth Five Year Plan, beginning in 1974.

s: In which year did the Tribal Sub-Plan, adopted in the Fifth Five Year Plan, originate?
x: The Tribal Sub-Plan originated in 1972 and was adopted in the Fifth Plan; its present form is DAPST.

s: Besides Special Central Assistance to the Tribal Sub-Plan, grants for tribal development flow to States under which constitutional provision?
x: Grants under Article 275(1), along with Special Central Assistance to TSP, fund tribal development. Article 282 covers discretionary grants, Article 280 the Finance Commission and Article 342(2) the ST list.

s: Which of the following statements regarding the Tribal Sub-Plan is correct?
o: It earmarks funds below the proportion of the ST population to prioritise general schemes.
It earmarks funds at least in proportion to the ST population, over and above normal plan flows.
It applies only to urban tribal populations.
It provides funds exclusively through private institutions.
x: TSP funds are to be at least proportional to the ST population and additional to normal plan flows or general benefits.

s: Scheduled Areas cover about what share of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Scheduled Areas cover 10.15 per cent of AP; STs number 27.39 lakh, 5.53 per cent of the population.

s: Scheduled Tribes constitute about 9% of the population but account for over what proportion of people displaced by development projects?
x: Scheduled Tribes constitute about 9 per cent of the population but account for over 50 per cent of people displaced by development projects.

s: Compared with the State average, tribal MMR and IMR in Andhra Pradesh are:
x: Both the tribal maternal mortality ratio and infant mortality rate are above the State average.

s: By what name is the Tribal Sub-Plan now known?
x: The TSP is now the Development Action Plan for STs (DAPST); DAPSC is the renamed SC plan.

s: Which State law, of 2013, was the first to make SC and Tribal Sub-Plan allocation binding?
x: The AP Scheduled Castes Sub-Plan and Tribal Sub-Plan Act, 2013 was the first State law making the allocation binding.

s: In which year was TRIFED, which runs Tribes India and gives MSP for minor forest produce, set up?
x: TRIFED dates from 1987; NSFDC is 1989, NSKFDC 1997 and NSTFDC 2001.

s: How many Scheduled Tribe communities are notified in Andhra Pradesh?
x: AP has 34 ST communities with 27.39 lakh people; 12 of them are PVTGs.

s: Which body handles self-employment schemes and rehabilitation of Jogins in Andhra Pradesh?
x: The AP SC Cooperative Finance Corporation handles self-employment and Jogin rehabilitation.

s: In which year was the Girijan Cooperative Corporation of Andhra Pradesh founded?
x: The GCC (1956) buys MFP at fair prices, runs PDS depots and gives credit to tribal farmers.

s: In which year was the Ministry of Tribal Affairs set up after being split from the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment?
x: The Ministry of Tribal Affairs was created in 1999 out of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.

s: From which date did the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes start functioning as a separate body?
x: The 89th Amendment (2003) split the SC/ST Commission; the separate NCST under Article 338A functions from 19 February 2004.

s: In which year was the Special Component Plan for Scheduled Castes, now called DAPSC, started?
x: The Special Component Plan began in 1979, was renamed SCSP and is now DAPSC; the TSP began in the Fifth Plan (1974).

s: The SHRESHTA Portal provides online CBT registration, merit evaluation and seat allotment for SC students in which type of institutions?
x: The SHRESHTA portal, run with NTA, handles online CBT registration, merit ranking and seat allotment for SC students in private residential schools.

s: The Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castes is associated with which of the following combinations?
o: Ministry of Finance; 2016-17; Rs 1 lakh to Rs 10 lakh
Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment; 2014-15; Rs 10 lakh to Rs 15 crore
Ministry of Tribal Affairs; 2001-02; Rs 10 lakh to Rs 1 crore
Ministry of Rural Development; 2013-14; Rs 15 lakh to Rs 25 crore
x: The Venture Capital Fund for SCs is under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, dates from 2014-15 and has a range of Rs 10 lakh to Rs 15 crore.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: TRIFED / Tribes India E-Marketplace – Marketplace for tribal artisans and forest-produce collectors
SHRESHTA Portal – Sickle Cell screening cards for tribal populations
PM-JANMAN Monitoring Dashboard – Saturation dashboard for 11 interventions across 75 PVTG communities
Sickle Cell Mission Portal – Tracking of sickle cell screening cards
x: SHRESHTA handles online CBT and seat allotment for SC students; sickle cell screening cards are tracked on the Sickle Cell Mission Portal.

s:
Assertion (A): Eklavya Model Residential Schools provide quality middle and high school education in remote areas.
Reason (R): An EMRS is to be set up in every block with more than 50% ST population and at least 20,000 tribal persons.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true: EMRS are sited in every block with over 50% ST population and at least 20,000 tribal persons, which are mostly remote areas, so R explains why they bring middle and high school education there.

s: Under which Ministry are Eklavya Model Residential Schools run as a Central Sector scheme?
o: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
x: EMRS is a Central Sector scheme under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about scholarships for SC and ST students?
o: The Post-Matric Scholarship for SCs is the largest central scheme for SC students
ST pre-matric and post-matric scholarships are centrally sponsored schemes
National Fellowship, Top Class and National Overseas are central sector schemes
The cost of the SC Post-Matric Scholarship is shared in the ratio 75:25
x: The SC Post-Matric Scholarship cost is shared in the ratio 60:40, not 75:25; the other statements are correct.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Stand-Up India?
o: It is meant exclusively for existing enterprises
Every bank branch is to lend to at least one SC/ST and one woman borrower
It is administered by the Ministry of Finance
x: Stand-Up India supports greenfield enterprises; it is not meant exclusively for existing enterprises.

s: To whom do the Dr Ambedkar Centres of Excellence give free Civil Services coaching?
x: The Dr Ambedkar Centres of Excellence give free Civil Services coaching to SC students in Central Universities.

s: In which year did the Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRS) scheme start?
x: EMRS began in 1997-98; its target is 740 schools and Odisha has the highest number of EMRS.

s: On which schools were Eklavya Model Residential Schools modelled?
x: EMRS were modelled on Navodaya Vidyalayas.

s: As per the norm, in which blocks is an EMRS to be set up?
o: More than 50% ST population and at least 20,000 tribal people
More than 40% ST population and at least 15,000 tribal people
More than 25% ST population and at least 10,000 tribal people
More than 60% ST population and at least 25,000 tribal people
x: The norm is one EMRS in every block with more than 50% ST population and at least 20,000 tribal people.

s: Which State has the most Eklavya Model Residential Schools?
x: Odisha has the most EMRS; the national target is 740 with 511 running (Aug 2026).

s: What is the loan range under Stand-Up India for greenfield enterprises?
x: Stand-Up India (5 April 2016) gives Rs 10 lakh to Rs 1 crore to SC/ST and women borrowers; Rs 10 lakh to Rs 15 crore is the VCF-SC range.

s: At which university were the Dr Ambedkar Centres of Excellence launched on 22 April 2022?
x: DACE gives Civil Services coaching in Central Universities and was launched at BHU.

s: How many National Overseas Scholarships are given each year for ST students?
x: There are 20 awards (17 ST and 3 PVTG) with a Rs 6 lakh income limit.

s: What is the target number of Eklavya Model Residential Schools to be set up in the country?
x: The EMRS target is 740 schools; about 511 were running by August 2026.

s: PM-AJAY, launched in 2021-22, is administered as a centrally sponsored intervention by which Union Ministry?
o: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
x: PM-AJAY was launched in 2021-22 as a 100 per cent centrally funded scheme under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.

s: Which is the nodal ministry for the Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan?
x: Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan is led by Tribal Affairs, which converges the work of several line ministries to bring basic facilities to tribal-majority villages.

s: The National Sickle Cell Elimination Mission is run by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare with the Ministry of:
x: The Mission is run by Health and Family Welfare with Tribal Affairs and focuses on screening tribal populations.

s: PM-JANMAN, launched in November 2023, covers how many Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups?
x: PM-JANMAN was launched in November 2023 for the development of 75 PVTGs.

s: How many Ministries are involved in the Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (September 2024)?
x: The Abhiyan involves 17 Ministries and covers about 63,000 tribal villages.

s: In PM-JANMAN (PM Janjati Adivasi ____ Maha Abhiyan), what does the letter 'N' stand for?
x: PM-JANMAN is the PM Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan for STs, especially PVTGs, with housing, roads, water and electricity.

s: PM-AJAY merges which of the following schemes or initiatives?
o: EMRS, PM-JANMAN, and Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan
Adarsh Gram, SCA to SCSP, and Babu Jagjivan Ram Chhatrawas Yojana
Naya Savera, Nai Udaan, and PM-VIKAS
x: PM-AJAY merges Adarsh Gram, Special Central Assistance to the SC Sub-Plan, and the Babu Jagjivan Ram hostel scheme, all for SCs. The other options are tribal, women's and minority schemes.

s: Which group does PM-AJAY aim to lift out of poverty?
x: PM-AJAY (2021-22, MoSJE) is a 100% central scheme that merged three SC schemes and targets SC poverty, not STs.

s: How many Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups are there in Andhra Pradesh?
x: AP has 12 PVTGs, including Chenchu, Bodo Gadaba, Konda Reddi and Kolam, out of 75 in India.

s: Which of the following is a PVTG of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Chenchu is among AP's 12 PVTGs; Bharia (MP) and Kamar and Baiga (Chhattisgarh) were the first PVTGs to get habitat rights.

s: Which of the following is NOT a criterion for identifying a PVTG?
x: PVTG criteria are pre-agricultural technology, low literacy, economic backwardness and a stagnant or declining population.

s: Over how many States and Union Territories are the 75 PVTGs of India spread?
x: The 75 PVTGs live in 18 States and 1 UT.

s: How many villages are covered under the Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan launched in September 2024?
x: Dharti Aaba (DAJGUA) covers about 63,000 villages with Rs 79,156 crore through 17 ministries.

s: By which year does the National Sickle Cell Elimination Mission aim to eliminate sickle cell disease?
x: The Sickle Cell Mission, run by the Health and Tribal Affairs ministries, targets elimination by 2047.

s: The PM Janjatiya Vikas Mission, associated with 2021-22, is run by TRIFED and includes which set of activities?
o: Civil Services coaching, NETS testing and residential schooling
PPE distribution, sewer profiling and sanitation stipends
Land purchase, pension payments and free electricity
Buying MFP at MSP, value addition and GI tags
x: The PM Janjatiya Vikas Mission is run by TRIFED and focuses on buying Minor Forest Produce at MSP, value addition and GI tags.

s: For what is the Roshni programme meant?
o: Free coaching for SC students in Central Universities
MSP procurement from all farmers in border districts
Mechanised cleaning of septic tanks in urban areas
Skills and jobs for tribal youth in Left-Wing Extremism districts
x: Roshni, associated with the Ministry of Rural Development and 2013, provides skills and employment opportunities for tribal youth in LWE districts.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about PM-AJAY?
o: Its portal supports planning and monitoring of works in SC-majority Adarsh Grams
It is targeted at Scheduled Castes
It is a portal for tribal artisans to sell forest produce
x: PM-AJAY plans, pools funds for and monitors works in SC-majority Adarsh Grams; the tribal artisans' marketplace is TRIFED/Tribes India.

s: In a Van Dhan Vikas Kendra, at least what share of members must be from Scheduled Tribes?
x: A Van Dhan Vikas Kendra typically has about 15 SHGs of up to 20 gatherers each, with at least 60% ST members.

s: Which initiative focuses on mechanized sanitation ecosystems, zero manual scavenging deaths and rehabilitation of sanitation workers?
x: NAMASTE, now with SMILE, aims at mechanised sanitation, zero deaths from manual scavenging, and rehabilitation of sanitation workers.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the NAMASTE portal?
o: It is associated with the Urban Affairs sector and Social Justice & Empowerment.
It digitally profiles sewer and septic-tank workers.
It conducts online CBT registration and seat allotment for SC students.
It supports health-insurance linkage and PPE verification.
x: Online CBT registration and seat allotment for SC students is done by the SHRESHTA portal; NAMASTE profiles sewer and septic-tank workers and links them to insurance and PPE.

s: What does the term 'Diku' mean in tribal usage?
o: An outsider-exploiter such as a moneylender, trader, landlord or contractor
x: Diku denotes an outsider-exploiter, including a moneylender, trader, landlord or contractor.

s: By what name do the Santhals revere Parasnath Hills, a Jain pilgrimage site?
x: Parasnath Hills are a Jain pilgrimage site and are revered by Santhals as Marang Buru.

s: Who identified political autonomy, recognition of identity and control over resources as objectives of modern tribal movements?
x: T. K. Oommen identified political autonomy, identity recognition and control over resources as objectives of modern tribal movements.

s: What is the first principle of Nehru's Panchsheel for tribal development?
o: Develop tribal people along the lines of their own genius
Impose a uniform administration on all tribal areas
Measure progress by the money spent
Assimilate tribal people rapidly into mainstream culture
x: The first principle is to develop tribal people along their own genius, respecting their distinct capacities and culture.

s: Which of the following is NOT a Panchsheel principle for tribal development?
o: Tribal rights in land and forests should be respected
Tribal people should be relied upon and trained for their own administration
Administration should be minimised and conducted through tribal institutions
Results should be judged by money spent rather than by the quality of human character evolved
x: Panchsheel requires results to be judged by the quality of human character evolved, not by money spent; the other three are Panchsheel principles.

s: Which of the following contributed to tribal indebtedness and land alienation during colonial rule?
x: Colonial moneylenders and revenue farmers contributed to indebtedness and land alienation, while restrictive forest laws cut tribals off from their habitats.

s: Which of the following pairs (Approach – Idea) relating to tribal policy is correctly matched?
o: Isolation – Development while retaining tribal identity
Assimilation – Tribes kept apart to protect their culture
Integration – Tribes treated as 'backward Hindus' and absorbed
Integration – Development while retaining tribal identity
x: Integration combines development with retention of identity; isolation keeps tribes apart to protect their culture, and assimilation absorbs them as 'backward Hindus'.

s: What is the source of Nehru's Panchsheel for tribal development?
o: Nehru’s foreword to Verrier Elwin’s A Philosophy for NEFA
x: The principles are sourced to Nehru’s foreword to Verrier Elwin’s work A Philosophy for NEFA.

s: Who is associated with the assimilation approach, which saw tribals as 'backward Hindus' to be absorbed?
x: G.S. Ghurye (with N.K. Bose) argued assimilation; early Elwin argued isolation and Nehru integration.

s: Who among the following is associated with the isolation ("national park") approach to tribal policy?
x: The early Verrier Elwin argued for keeping tribals apart; Ghurye favoured assimilation and Nehru integration.

s:
Match the following:
List-I (Approach)
A. Isolation
B. Assimilation
C. Integration
List-II (Proponent)
1. Jawaharlal Nehru
2. G.S. Ghurye
3. Early Verrier Elwin
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Isolation is linked with the early Elwin, assimilation with Ghurye and integration with Nehru.

s: Against what was Birsa Munda's Ulgulan directed?
o: Only forest conservation by tribal institutions
The Panchsheel principles of tribal development
x: Birsa’s Ulgulan was aimed at British land-grabbing and the exploitative dikus.

s: Birsa Munda is also known by which title?
x: Birsa Munda is popularly known as Dharti Aaba.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Birsa Munda's Ulgulan?
o: Its objective included the establishment of Abua Raj
It opposed land-grabbing and forced labour
It led to the enactment of the Chotanagpur Tenancy Act, 1876
x: The Ulgulan led to the Chotanagpur Tenancy Act of 1908, not 1876; the other statements are correct.

s: Which of the following tribal revolt–leader pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Srikakulam Girijan movement (1967-70) – Alluri Sitarama Raju
x: The Srikakulam Girijan movement was led by Vempatapu Satyanarayana and Adibhatla Kailasam; Alluri Sitarama Raju led the Rampa rebellion.

s:
Arrange the following tribal movements in chronological order:
A. Srikakulam Girijan movement
B. Santhal Hul
C. Rampa rebellion
D. Birsa’s Ulgulan
x: The correct sequence is Santhal Hul (1855–56), Birsa’s Ulgulan (1899–1900), Rampa rebellion (1922–24), and Srikakulam Girijan movement (1967–70).

s: Who led the Santhal Hul (1855-56) against the dikus?
x: Sidhu and Kanhu led the Santhal Hul; Birsa led the Ulgulan, Alluri the Rampa rebellion and Vempatapu the Srikakulam movement.

s: Which law was enacted as a result of Birsa Munda's Ulgulan?
o: AP Scheduled Areas Land Transfer Regulation, 1959
x: The Ulgulan (1899-1900), aiming at Abua Raj, led to the Chotanagpur Tenancy Act, 1908.

s: Who among the following led the Srikakulam Girijan movement (1967-70)?
x: The Srikakulam Girijan movement was led by Vempatapu Satyanarayana and Adibhatla Kailasam; Alluri led the Rampa rebellion.

s: Against what was the Rampa rebellion (1922-24) led by Alluri Sitarama Raju mainly directed?
x: The Rampa rebellion arose from colonial forest curbs on podu (shifting) cultivation.

s: What is the main aim of the Andhra Pradesh Scheduled Areas Land Transfer Regulation, 1959?
o: Bar transfer of land in Scheduled Areas to non-tribals
Transfer all Scheduled Area land to the Union Government
Facilitate transfer of tribal land to private mining companies
x: Regulation 1 of 1959 bars the transfer of land in Scheduled Areas to non-tribals.

s: What did the 1970 amendment to the AP Scheduled Areas Land Transfer Regulation add?
o: Removal of the bar on land transfers to non-tribals
A presumption that land belongs to tribals and a bar on transfers even between non-tribals
Permission for transfers approved by a private company
Application of the Regulation only to urban municipal areas
x: Regulation 1 of 1970 presumed Scheduled Area land to be tribal and barred transfers even between non-tribals.

s: What did the Supreme Court hold in Samatha v. State of Andhra Pradesh (1997)?
o: The AP land transfer regulation does not apply to mining leases
Government land in Scheduled Areas may always be leased to private mining companies
Leasing tribal or government land in Scheduled Areas to non-tribals or private mining companies is void
Only tribal cooperatives are prohibited from mining in Scheduled Areas
x: The Samatha judgment held that land in Scheduled Areas cannot be transferred or leased to non-tribals or private companies, including private mining companies.

s: In which year did the Supreme Court strike down G.O. No. 3 (2000), which gave 100% of Scheduled Area teacher posts to local STs?
x: G.O. No. 3 was issued in 2000 and struck down by the Supreme Court in 2020.

s: Since the State cannot lease Scheduled Area land to non-tribals, to whom is mining in AP Scheduled Areas left?
o: Private companies with Gram Sabha consent
Any company approved by the Centre
Non-tribal individuals holding up to 4 ha
x: The State cannot lease Scheduled Area land to non-tribals, so mining is left to State undertakings or tribal cooperatives; Gram Sabha consent does not validate a private lease.

s: The Koya and Kondh communities oppose which project over land rights, poor compensation and displacement without proper rehabilitation?
x: The Koya and Kondh communities oppose the Polavaram project over land rights, inadequate compensation and displacement without rehabilitation.

s: What were the main demands of the tribal bandh in the Alluri Sitarama Raju district?
o: Abolition of PESA and continuation of G.O. 3
Strict enforcement of the 1/70 law and a replacement for G.O. 3
Removal of the Fifth Schedule and expansion of mining surveys
Transfer of forest rights exclusively to private companies
x: The bandh demanded strict enforcement of 1/70 and a replacement for G.O. 3.

s: In PESA areas of Andhra Pradesh, at least what share of seats is reserved for Scheduled Tribes?
x: In PESA areas at least 50 per cent of seats go to STs and all chairpersons are STs.

s: Which of the 10 PESA States has only draft PESA rules?
x: Nine of the 10 PESA States, including Andhra Pradesh, have framed PESA rules; Odisha has only draft rules.

s: To which areas does the PESA Act, 1996 extend Part IX of the Constitution?
x: PESA extends the Panchayat provisions of Part IX to Fifth Schedule (Scheduled) areas.

s: Under the AP PESA Rules, 2011, how many PESA Gram Sabhas are there in Andhra Pradesh?
x: Andhra Pradesh has 2,038 PESA Gram Sabhas under its 2011 PESA Rules.

s: Of which scheme is the dashboard for 11 critical interventions across 75 PVTG communities a part?
x: The 11-intervention dashboard for 75 PVTGs is PM-JANMAN; Hunar Haat/PM-VIKAS promotes minority artisans.

s: What is the cost-sharing pattern for Samagra Shiksha?
o: 100:0 generally and 90:10 for North-Eastern and hill States
40:60 generally and 10:90 for North-Eastern and hill States
60:40 generally and 90:10 for North-Eastern and hill States
50:50 generally and 75:25 for North-Eastern and hill States
x: The Centre-State sharing pattern is 60:40 generally and 90:10 for North-Eastern and hill States.

s: Samagra Shiksha (2018) merged Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan, Rashtriya Madhyamik Shiksha Abhiyan and which other scheme?
x: Samagra Shiksha merged SSA, RMSA and Teacher Education into one school education scheme.

s: In which year was Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan, later merged into Samagra Shiksha, launched?
x: SSA began in 2001 and was merged into Samagra Shiksha in 2018; 1968 was the first NPE and 1975 the start of ICDS.

s: In what ratio are Samagra Shiksha funds shared between the Centre and the North-Eastern and hill States?
x: Samagra Shiksha is funded 60:40, and 90:10 for North-Eastern and hill States.

s: In which year was India's first National Policy on Education adopted?
x: The first National Policy on Education came in 1968; universal elementary education is one of its priority areas.

s: Up to which class do Kasturba Gandhi Balika Vidyalayas (KGBVs) run under Samagra Shiksha?
x: Under Samagra Shiksha, KGBVs have been extended up to Class 12.

s: What did the Supreme Court recognise for children below 14 years in Unni Krishnan v. State of Andhra Pradesh (1993)?
o: A right to employment in non-hazardous industries
A statutory right to adoption under Article 24
A fundamental duty to provide education under Article 51A(k)
A fundamental right to free education under Article 21
x: Unni Krishnan recognised a fundamental right to free education for children below 14 years under Article 21. The decision formed the basis for the later insertion of Article 21A.

s: The Supreme Court has described quality elementary teacher education as vital to realising which Article?
x: The Supreme Court stressed that quality elementary teacher education is vital to Article 21A, the constitutional right to education.

s: Which case upheld the 25 per cent quota in unaided private schools, while excluding unaided minority schools from its application?
o: Bachpan Bachao Andolan v. Union of India
Unni Krishnan v. State of AP
Pramati Educational and Cultural Trust v. Union of India
Society for Unaided Private Schools of Rajasthan v. Union of India
x: Society for Unaided Private Schools of Rajasthan v. Union of India (2012) upheld the 25 per cent quota in unaided private schools, but not in unaided minority schools.

s: Which case held that the RTE Act does not apply to minority schools?
o: Pramati Educational and Cultural Trust v. Union of India
Unni Krishnan v. State of Andhra Pradesh
Mohini Jain v. State of Karnataka
Bachpan Bachao Andolan v. Union of India
x: Pramati excluded aided and unaided minority schools from the RTE Act; Bachpan Bachao Andolan dealt with trafficking, circus children and FIRs on missing children.

s: The Unni Krishnan case (1993) on the right to free education arose from which State?
x: Unni Krishnan v. State of AP arose from Andhra Pradesh and held children below 14 have a right to free education under Article 21.

s: What did Bachpan Bachao Andolan v. Union of India (2011) deal with?
o: The 25 per cent quota in private schools
Child trafficking and children in circuses
The right to free education under Article 21
x: Bachpan Bachao Andolan dealt with child trafficking and children in circuses, with FIRs for missing children.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The RTE Act, 2009 came into force on 1 April 2010.
2. The 2019 amendment to the RTE Act allowed regular examinations in Classes 5 and 8.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The RTE Act came into force on 1 April 2010; the 2019 amendment brought exams in Classes 5 and 8 and allowed detention after a re-exam.

s: Section 12(1)(c) of the Right to Education Act relates to which of the following?
o: Reservation of 50% seats in private schools for all children
Reservation of 25% seats in all government colleges for girls
Reservation of 25% entry-level seats in unaided private schools for specified children
Reservation of 35% seats in aided schools for minorities
x: Section 12(1)(c) requires unaided private schools, excluding minority institutions, to reserve 25% of entry-level seats for children from weaker sections and disadvantaged groups.

s: In which year was the RTE Act amended to permit detention at Classes V and VIII subject to safeguards?
x: The original Act barred detention up to Class VIII; the 2019 amendment allowed detention at Classes V and VIII after examinations and a re-examination opportunity.

s: Which pupil-teacher ratio is prescribed under the RTE norms?
x: The prescribed pupil-teacher ratio is 30:1 at the primary level and 35:1 at the upper-primary level.

s: Under the RTE Act, 2009, what proportion of the members of a School Management Committee must be parents or guardians?
x: Three-fourths of SMC members must be parents or guardians; SMCs are provided under Section 21 in every government and aided school.

s: Which of the following lies outside the statutory entitlement of the RTE Act, 2009?
o: Neighbourhood schools for children aged 6 to 14
x: The RTE Act covers free and compulsory elementary education (6-14, Classes 1-8); pre-school and secondary education are not included.

s: Under the RTE Act, to which class is an out-of-school child to be admitted?
o: The lowest class of the nearest school
A class decided by a screening test
x: The RTE Act provides age-appropriate admission for out-of-school children and prohibits screening and capitation fee.

s: Which body does monitoring and grievance redressal under the RTE Act at the national level?
o: National Council of Educational Research and Training
National Commission for Protection of Child Rights
x: NCPCR and the State Commissions monitor and redress grievances under the RTE Act; SMCs are school-level bodies.

s: Which of the following pairs relating to the RTE Act, 2009 is correctly matched?
x: The RTE Act gives effect to Article 21A, covers children aged 6-14 (Classes 1-8) and came into force on 1 April 2010.

s: Which authority lays down the minimum qualifications for appointment of teachers under the RTE framework?
o: State Council for Teacher Education alone
National Commission for Protection of Child Rights
x: The minimum teacher qualifications are laid down by the academic authority notified by the Central Government, namely the National Council for Teacher Education (NCTE).

s: Under which Section of the RTE Act, 2009 does the appropriate Government make rules, such as the State RTE Rules?
x: Section 38 lets the appropriate Government make rules; States frame their RTE Rules and admission rules under it.

s: Which of the following does the RTE Act, 2009 prohibit at the time of admission?
o: Screening of the child and capitation fee
Admission of an out-of-school child to an age-appropriate class
Reimbursement of 25 per cent quota seats by the State
x: The RTE Act bars any screening procedure and capitation fee for admission.

s:
Consider the following statements about the RTE Act, 2009:
1. A school cannot collect a capitation fee for admission.
2. A school may hold a screening test for admission to Class 1.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Act bars both capitation fees and screening of children for admission, so only statement 1 is correct.

s: Which of the following is NOT one of the four core principles of the UNCRC?
o: Right to life, survival and development
x: The four core principles are non-discrimination, best interests of the child, life-survival-development and respect for the child's views; free secondary education is not one of them.

s: On which date did the UN General Assembly adopt the Convention on the Rights of the Child?
x: The UN General Assembly adopted the UNCRC on 20 November 1989.

s: Survival, development and protection are three of the four broad categories of rights under the UNCRC. Which is the fourth?
x: The four categories are survival, development, protection and participation; education is not a separate category.

s: In which year did India ratify the two 2000 Optional Protocols to the UNCRC?
x: India ratified the two 2000 Optional Protocols in 2005 but is not a party to the 2011 Communications Procedure Protocol.

s: The UN Convention on the Rights of the Child contains how many articles?
x: The UNCRC (20 November 1989) has 54 articles; India acceded on 11 December 1992.

s: On which date is Universal Children's Day observed?
x: 20 November is Universal Children's Day and the UNCRC adoption date; 14 November is India's Children's Day.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Optional Protocols to the UNCRC:
1. India ratified the two 2000 Optional Protocols in 2005.
2. India is a party to the 2011 Protocol on a communications procedure.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Only 1 is correct: India ratified both 2000 Protocols in 2005 but is not a party to the 2011 communications procedure Protocol.

s: In which year did India accede to the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child?
x: India acceded to the UNCRC on 11 December 1992; it ratified the two 2000 Optional Protocols in 2005.

s: The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) was set up in which year, under which law?
o: 2007, under the Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005
x: NCPCR was set up in 2007 under the CPCR Act, 2005. The JJ Act, RTE Act and POCSO Act are laws it monitors, not its parent law.

s: What is the composition of the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights?
o: Only a Chairperson and members nominated by the Supreme Court
A Chairperson and eight members, including three women
A Chairperson and six members, including at least two women
A Chairperson and four members, including one woman
x: The NCPCR consists of a Chairperson and six members, of whom at least two must be women. It is not composed solely of judicial nominees.

s: Who was the first Chairperson of the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (2007)?
x: The NCPCR was set up in 2007 with Shanta Sinha as its first chairperson.

s: While inquiring into complaints, the NCPCR has the powers of which court?
x: The NCPCR has civil-court powers while inquiring into complaints.

s: Besides the JJ Act, 2015 and the RTE Act, 2009, which Act does the NCPCR specifically monitor?
x: NCPCR monitors the JJ Act 2015, POCSO Act 2012 and RTE Act 2009, not the Child Labour Amendment Act 2016 or its own parent law.

s: Which platform provides real-time digital tracking of Anganwadi service delivery, stunting, wasting and nutrition metrics for children aged 0–6 years?
x: The Poshan Tracker app (WCD) tracks Anganwadi services, stunting, wasting and nutrition for children aged 0–6 in real time.

s: For what is the CARINGS portal used?
o: Tracking of Anganwadi services and nutrition metrics
Citizen reporting of missing and sighted children
Tracking missing, vulnerable and institutionalised children
Child adoption referrals and status tracking
x: CARINGS handles adoption referrals; Poshan Tracker tracks nutrition, TrackChild traces missing children and Khoya-Paya takes citizen reports.

s: Which portal enables citizens to report missing or sighted children?
x: Khoya-Paya supports citizen reporting of missing or sighted children; TrackChild tracks missing and found children and CARINGS relates to adoption.

s: What is CHILDLINE 1098?
o: An online portal exclusively for cybercrime complaints
A statutory commission for monitoring the RTE Act
A 24×7 child helpline integrated with ERSS-112
A judicial body for transferring juveniles aged 16–18 years
x: CHILDLINE 1098 is a 24×7 child helpline and is now integrated with ERSS-112.

s: CHILDLINE 1098 has been integrated with which emergency response number?
x: CHILDLINE 1098 is integrated with ERSS-112 across 36 States/UTs.

s: Under which mission does TrackChild, which tracks missing and found children, work?
x: TrackChild is a Women and Child Development portal under Mission Vatsalya.

s: With which of the following is e-Baal Nidan associated?
o: Online complaints regarding violation of child rights
Tracking children rescued from hazardous employment only
x: e-Baal Nidan is the NCPCR’s online complaint portal for violations of child rights. CARINGS is the adoption-related system, while CHILDLINE 1098 is the emergency helpline.

s: Which Article of the Constitution contains the duty of parents to provide education to children aged 6-14 years?
x: The parental duty is a Fundamental Duty under Article 51A(k); Article 39(e) protects the tender age of children from abuse.

s: Which Constitutional Amendment reworded Article 39(f) on the healthy development of children in freedom and dignity?
x: Article 39(f) was reworded by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976. The 86th Amendment is associated with Articles 21A, 45 and 51A(k).

s: Which Article of the Constitution prohibits employment of children below 14 years in factories, mines or other hazardous employment?
x: Article 24 bars children below 14 from factories, mines and hazardous employment. Article 23 bans traffic in human beings and forced labour, Article 39(e) is a Directive Principle against abuse of tender age, and Article 21A is the right to education.

s: Which Constitutional Amendment first made education a Fundamental Right?
x: The 86th Amendment (2002) made education a Fundamental Right.

s: Which Article of the Constitution permits special provisions for women and children?
x: Article 15(3), in the original Constitution, allows special provisions for women and children.

s: Which Article of the Constitution prohibits traffic in human beings and forced labour?
x: Article 23 bans traffic in human beings and forced labour; Article 24 bars children below 14 from factories and mines.
