s: Which Article directs that the tender age of children is not abused and that they are not forced by economic necessity into unsuited avocations?
x: Article 39(e) protects the tender age of children; 39(f) concerns healthy development in freedom and dignity.

s: Which Article of the Constitution, as substituted by the 86th Amendment, provides for early childhood care and education for children up to six years?
x: The 86th Amendment rewrote Article 45 to cover early childhood care and education till age six.

s: Under which Act did the Central Adoption Resource Authority (CARA) become a statutory body?
o: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
x: CARA became a statutory body under the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015.

s: Which statement correctly distinguishes the two principal legal routes of adoption?
o: HAMA applies to specified religious communities, whereas the JJ route is open to all religions
HAMA is open to all religions, whereas the JJ route is restricted to Hindus
Both HAMA and the JJ route are restricted to Hindus
Neither route permits adoption by persons belonging to different religions
x: HAMA applies to Hindus, Buddhists, Jains and Sikhs, while the adoption route under the Juvenile Justice Act is open to all religions.

s: On which date did the POCSO Act, 2012 come into force?
x: The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act came into force on 14 November 2012 and defines a child as below 18.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the POCSO Act, 2012?
o: It defines a child as a person below 18
Its 2019 Amendment provides death penalty for aggravated penetrative sexual assault
It came into force on 14 November 2012
x: The 2019 Amendment, notified 16 August 2019, provides death penalty for aggravated penetrative sexual assault on children; POCSO is gender-neutral.

s: The Criminal Law (Amendment) Ordinance, April 2018 made death penalty possible for rape of a girl below what age?
x: The April 2018 Ordinance allowed death penalty for rape of a girl below 12.

s: Under the JJ Act, 2015, who makes the preliminary assessment of a 16-18 year old accused of a heinous offence?
x: The Juvenile Justice Board makes the preliminary assessment; the case may then go to the Children's Court to be tried as an adult.

s: Under the JJ Act, 2015, which body deals with children in need of care and protection?
x: Child Welfare Committees handle children in need of care and protection; JJBs deal with children in conflict with law.

s: After the 2021 amendment to the JJ Act, who issues adoption orders?
x: The 2021 amendment, in force from 1 September 2022, empowers the District Magistrate to issue adoption orders.

s: To which of the following does the Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956 NOT apply?
x: HAMA covers Hindus, Buddhists, Jains and Sikhs; the JJ Act route is open to all religions.

s: Under the Adoption Regulations, 2022, what reconsideration period do a surrendered child's parents get?
x: The Adoption Regulations 2022 give a 2-month reconsideration period for a surrendered child.

s: In which year was India's first Juvenile Justice law enacted?
x: The first Juvenile Justice Act was passed in 1986; it was followed by the JJ Acts of 2000 and 2015.

s: Under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, what is needed to process the personal data of a child below 18 years?
o: Order of a Juvenile Justice Board
x: The DPDP Act 2023 treats anyone below 18 as a child and requires verifiable consent of a parent or guardian.

s: Which of the following correctly compares the age thresholds under POCSO, the child labour law and the RTE Act?
o: POCSO: below 21; child labour law: below 16; RTE: 6–14 years
POCSO: below 14; child labour law: below 18; RTE: 6–18 years
POCSO: 6–14 years; child labour law: below 18; RTE: below 14 years
POCSO: below 18; child labour law: below 14; RTE: 6–14 years
x: POCSO defines a child as below 18 years, child labour law uses the below-14 threshold stated here, and RTE covers children aged 6–14 years.

s: Survival, health and nutrition; education and development; and protection are three priority areas of the National Policy for Children, 2013. Which is the fourth?
x: The fourth priority area of NPC 2013 is participation; vocational employment is not one of them.

s: What did the National Plan of Action for Children, 2016 mainly do?
o: Introduced the constitutional right to education
Replaced the National Policy for Children, 2013
Limited child protection to the education sector
Operationalised the National Policy for Children, 2013
x: The National Plan of Action for Children, 2016 put the National Policy for Children, 2013 into operation. It follows the same four priority areas.

s: Below what age is a person a child under the National Policy for Children, 2013?
x: The National Policy for Children, adopted in April 2013, treats every person below 18 as a child. 14 is the threshold of child labour law and Article 24, 16 is an age-of-consent figure that has been debated, and 21 is the marriage age for men.

s: Which was the first child labour law in India?
o: Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009
x: The 1933 Children (Pledging of Labour) Act was the first child labour law; the 1986 Act was the first comprehensive one.

s: In which year was India's first National Policy for Children adopted?
x: The first National Policy for Children was in 1974; NPC 2013 replaced it.

s: What is the name of the 100-day campaign against child marriage launched from December 2025?
x: Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat is a 100-day campaign against child marriage that began in December 2025.

s: What was India's child sex ratio (0-6 years) as per the provisional Census 2011 figures?
x: The child sex ratio (0-6) was 914 in Census 2011. 943 is the overall sex ratio in Census 2011, and 1,020 is the overall sex ratio in NFHS-5. 927 was the child sex ratio in Census 2001.

s: Which of the following indicator–figure pairs is correctly matched?
x: The overall sex ratio was 943 in Census 2011; 914 was the provisional child sex ratio and 1,020 the NFHS-5 figure.

s: As per Census 2011, about how many child main workers aged 5-14 were there?
x: Census 2011 counted 4.35 million child main workers; about 10.1 million including marginal workers.

s: According to NFHS-5, what is the Total Fertility Rate of India?
x: NFHS-5 recorded India's TFR at 2.0.

s: According to NFHS-5, what is the infant mortality rate (per 1,000 live births) of India?
x: NFHS-5 gives IMR as 35.2 and under-five mortality as 41.9.

s: For enforcement of which law is the PENCIL portal mainly meant?
o: The Right to Education Act, 2009 only
The amended Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986
The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 only
x: PENCIL is the online portal for effective enforcement of the amended Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986.

s: The offence of trafficking of persons, widened by the Criminal Law Amendment Act 2013, is now dealt with under which provision?
o: Section 370, Indian Penal Code, which continues in force
x: Trafficking is now Section 143 of the BNS 2023. Section 63 BNS is the rape provision that keeps the age of consent at 18; Section 19 POCSO concerns mandatory reporting; the IPC was replaced by the BNS from 1 July 2024.

s: In which year was the National Child Labour Project started?
x: The National Child Labour Project was started in 1988.

s: According to Census 2011, approximately how many child labourers in the 5-14 age group were there in India?
x: Census 2011 recorded approximately 10.1 million child labourers aged 5–14. The 4.35 million figure refers only to main workers.

s: Which statement best reflects the relationship between child labour and abuse in India?
o: Debt bondage affects only adults and cannot involve children
Child labour is unrelated to exploitation when the child works within the family
Debt bondage in child labour can run across generations, and India has the largest number of child labourers in the world
India has no significant child-labour problem outside hazardous industries
x: Child labour is recognised as a form of abuse; India is described as having the largest number of child labourers in the world, with debt bondage extending across generations.

s: According to Census 2011, how many main workers were there among child labourers aged 5–14?
x: Census 2011 counted 10.1 million child labourers (5–14) including marginal workers, of whom 4.35 million were main workers.

s: Which country has the largest number of child labourers in the world?
x: India has the largest number of child labourers, driven by poverty, demand for cheap labour and debt bondage.

s: According to Census 2011, which State had the largest number of child labourers aged 5-14?
x: Census 2011 shows Uttar Pradesh with the most child workers, about 21.8 lakh.

s: According to Census 2011, about what share of India's child labourers aged 5-14 were in Uttar Pradesh?
x: About 21.8 lakh of India's 1.01 crore child workers, roughly one in five, were in Uttar Pradesh.

s: What is the expanded form of PENCIL in the context of child labour enforcement?
o: Platform for Effective Enforcement for No Child Labour
Public Enforcement Network for Child Labour
Programme for Effective Enforcement of National Child Labour
Platform for Elimination of Child Labour and Exploitation
x: PENCIL stands for Platform for Effective Enforcement for No Child Labour, run by the Ministry of Labour.

s: With which of the following are Operation Smile and Operation Muskaan mainly associated?
x: These MHA-led drives trace and rescue missing children.

s: Which law widened the concept of trafficking to include sexual exploitation, slavery, servitude, forced labour and organ removal?
x: The Criminal Law Amendment Act, 2013 widened trafficking to cover sexual exploitation, slavery, servitude, forced labour and organ removal.

s: Which of the following is NOT a component of the PENCIL portal?
x: The listed PENCIL components include the Child Tracking System, Complaint Corner, State Government, NCLP and Convergence. National Adoption Registry is not one of them.

s: What is the main objective of the National Child Labour Project?
o: Transfer all rescued children directly to juvenile courts
Regulate adult employment in hazardous industries
Withdraw children from labour and provide education and vocational training
Provide only financial compensation to employers
x: The NCLP withdraws children from labour and provides education and vocational training.

s: Which age group of rescued children do Special Training Centres under the National Child Labour Project cater to?
x: NCLP Special Training Centres serve rescued children aged 9-14 with bridge education, vocational training, mid-day meal and a stipend.

s: What is the helpline number of CHILDLINE, which is integrated with ERSS-112?
x: CHILDLINE 1098 is integrated with the Emergency Response Support System 112.

s: In which year was the PENCIL portal for child labour enforcement launched?
x: PENCIL was launched in 2017 by the Ministry of Labour and Employment.

s: For which cases is PENCIL an inter-agency tracking mechanism?
x: PENCIL tracks child labour cases by linking Child Labour Committees, police and NGOs for rescue and rehabilitation.

s: Which Ministry runs the National Child Labour Project?
o: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
x: The NCLP is run by the Ministry of Labour and Employment, not the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.

s: Which one of the following cases held that child labour in construction violates fundamental rights?
o: M.C. Mehta v. State of Tamil Nadu (1996)
Bachpan Bachao Andolan v. Union of India (2011)
x: PUDR v. Union of India (1982) held that child labour in construction violates fundamental rights.

s: Which judgement banned child labour in hazardous industries and mandated a Child Labour Rehabilitation-cum-Welfare Fund?
o: M.C. Mehta v. State of Tamil Nadu
Bachpan Bachao Andolan v. Union of India
Independent Thought v. Union of India
x: M.C. Mehta v. State of Tamil Nadu (1996) banned child labour in hazardous industries and ordered a Child Labour Rehabilitation-cum-Welfare Fund. Bachpan Bachao Andolan (2011) was about trafficking and child begging.

s: Which of the following case–subject pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: M.C. Mehta v. State of Tamil Nadu – Child labour in hazardous industries
Bachpan Bachao Andolan v. Union of India – Child trafficking and child begging
M.C. Mehta v. State of Tamil Nadu – Consensual same-sex adult relationships
Bachpan Bachao Andolan v. Union of India – Human-rights oversight of Child Care Institutions
x: M.C. Mehta v. State of Tamil Nadu dealt with hazardous child labour; consensual same-sex relations was the subject of Navtej Johar.

s: In M.C. Mehta v. State of Tamil Nadu, the offending employer had to deposit how much per child in the Child Labour Rehabilitation-cum-Welfare Fund?
x: The employer was directed to deposit ₹20,000 for each child into the Child Labour Rehabilitation-cum-Welfare Fund.

s: What does ILO Convention No. 182 concern?
x: ILO Convention No. 182 deals with the Worst Forms of Child Labour; Convention No. 138 deals with the Minimum Age for Employment.

s: Which judgement struck down the marital-rape exception in IPC Section 375 for wives below 18?
o: Bachpan Bachao Andolan v. Union of India
Independent Thought v. Union of India
Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India
M.C. Mehta v. State of Tamil Nadu
x: Independent Thought (2017) struck down the exception, holding sex with a girl under 18 is statutory rape even within marriage.

s: On which date is the World Day Against Child Labour observed?
x: The World Day Against Child Labour is observed on 12 June.

s: On which date did India ratify ILO Conventions 138 and 182?
x: India ratified both conventions on 13 June 2017; 12 June is World Day Against Child Labour.

s: Which case dealt with trafficking, child begging and circus children, with oversight of child care institutions?
o: M.C. Mehta v. State of Tamil Nadu (1996)
Independent Thought v. Union of India (2017)
x: Bachpan Bachao Andolan (2011) covered trafficking, child begging and circus children.

s: M.C. Mehta v. State of Tamil Nadu (1996) arose from child labour in which place?
x: The case concerned Sivakasi and banned child labour in hazardous industries.

s: What is the subject of ILO Convention No. 138?
o: Minimum age for admission to employment
x: ILO Convention 138 (1973) is on minimum age for employment; Convention 182 (1999) is on the worst forms of child labour.

s:
Match the following:
List-I (ILO Convention)
A. Convention 138
B. Convention 182
List-II (Subject)
1. Worst forms of child labour
2. Minimum age for employment
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Convention 138 sets the minimum age for employment and Convention 182 covers the worst forms of child labour; India ratified both on 13 June 2017.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. ILO Conventions 138 and 182 are among the eight fundamental ILO conventions.
2. India ratified both these conventions in 2017.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Conventions 138 (minimum age) and 182 (worst forms) are fundamental ILO conventions; India ratified both on 13 June 2017.

s: Which Ministry launched the PENCIL portal?
o: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
Ministry of Women and Child Development
x: The PENCIL portal was launched by the Ministry of Labour and Employment.

s: Under the JJ Act, 2015, for which offences may children aged 16-18 be tried as adults?
o: Any offence punishable with fine only
x: The JJ Act, 2015 lets 16–18-year-olds be tried as adults only for heinous offences.

s: The Juvenile Justice Act, 2015 made registration of which institutions compulsory?
x: The Act made registration compulsory for all Child Care Institutions.

s: Under the JJ Act, 2015, which body deals with a Child in Need of Care and Protection?
x: A Child in Need of Care and Protection goes to the Child Welfare Committee; a Child in Conflict with Law goes to the Juvenile Justice Board.

s: The Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 replaced the term ‘juvenile’ with which term?
x: The Act replaced the term ‘juvenile’ with ‘child’, reflecting a child-centred approach.

s: Under the JJ Act, 2015, what minimum punishment makes an offence a 'heinous offence'?
x: A heinous offence is defined by a minimum punishment of seven years or more.

s: After a preliminary assessment of a 16-18 year old accused of a heinous offence, to which court may the Juvenile Justice Board transfer the case?
x: The JJB may transfer the matter to the Children's Court after the preliminary assessment, which does not itself establish guilt.

s: The Juvenile Justice (Amendment) Act, 2021 made whom the focal point for implementation of the Act and empowered to decide adoption cases?
o: Chairperson of the Child Welfare Committee
Principal Magistrate of the Juvenile Justice Board
x: The 2021 amendment made the District Magistrate the focal point for implementation and gave the DM power to decide adoption cases.

s: At what age was the juvenile age made uniform under the JJ (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2000?
x: The JJ Act, 2000 prescribed a uniform age of 18 years and was amended in 2006.

s: Which event led to the punitive turn in the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015?
o: The Delhi gang rape case of 2012
The enactment of the CPCR Act in 2005
x: The 2015 Act followed the punitive policy response triggered by the Delhi gang rape case of 2012.

s: Which Act gave statutory status to the Central Adoption Resource Authority (CARA)?
o: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015
Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005
x: The JJ Act 2015 made CARA a statutory body. HAMA 1956 is a separate adoption route for Hindus, Buddhists, Jains and Sikhs; the 2021 amendment gave District Magistrates the power to decide adoptions; the CPCR Act 2005 created the NCPCR.

s: Which body deals with Children in Conflict with Law?
o: National Commission for Protection of Child Rights
x: Children in Conflict with Law come before Juvenile Justice Boards; every district has both a JJB and a CWC, each with at least one woman member.

s: What is the composition of a Juvenile Justice Board?
o: A Sessions Judge and four police officers
A Principal Magistrate and two social workers, at least one of whom is a woman
A Chairperson and four members, all of whom must be social workers
A District Magistrate and five elected representatives
x: The Board comprises a Metropolitan Magistrate or Judicial Magistrate First Class serving as Principal Magistrate and two social workers, with at least one woman among the social workers.

s: What kind of court is the Children's Court that tries cases transferred by the Juvenile Justice Board?
o: Court of the Judicial Magistrate First Class
x: The Children's Court is a Sessions Court that tries cases transferred to it; the Board handles children in conflict with law.

s: What is the guiding principle in proceedings involving children under the juvenile justice system?
o: Best interests of the child through child-friendly and rehabilitation-oriented justice
Detention in every case until adulthood
Retributive punishment as the primary objective
x: The system is guided by the best interests of the child and follows child-friendly, rehabilitation-oriented justice rather than a punishment-centred approach.

s: How are working children treated under the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015?
o: Adult workers requiring wage protection only
Children in conflict with law in every case
Children in need of care and protection
x: The Juvenile Justice Act, 2015 treats working children as children in need of care and protection.

s: A Private Member's Bill of December 2025 sought to lower the heinous-offence age threshold in the juvenile justice law from what to what?
x: The Bill sought to lower the heinous-offence threshold from 16 years to 14 years.

s: At what ages did the Juvenile Justice Act, 1986 fix the juvenile age for boys and girls respectively?
x: The 1986 Act, the first uniform juvenile law, set 16 for boys and 18 for girls; the 2000 Act made it 18 for all.

s: For which areas was the Children Act, 1960 enacted?
x: The Children Act, 1960 applied to the Union Territories.

s: Under the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015, a Child Welfare Committee has a Chairperson and how many members?
x: A CWC has a Chairperson and 4 members; a JJB has a Principal Magistrate and 2 social workers.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the preliminary assessment under the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015?
o: It applies to 16–18-year-olds accused of heinous offences
It is made by the Juvenile Justice Board
It may lead to transfer of the case to the Children's Court
It amounts to a finding of guilt
x: The preliminary assessment is not a finding of guilt; it only decides whether the case may go to the Children's Court.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015:
1. It came into force on 15 January 2016.
2. Its 2021 amendment came into force on 1 September 2022.
3. Every district has a Juvenile Justice Board and a Child Welfare Committee.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: All three are correct: in force 15 Jan 2016, 2021 amendment in force 1 Sept 2022, and a JJB and CWC in every district.

s: Besides the JJ Act, 2015, Andhra Pradesh's juvenile justice system follows which law?
x: AP follows the JJ Act, 2015 along with the Probation of Offenders Act, 1958; its JJBs are headed by a female Principal Magistrate.

s: The Draft National Policy on Child Protection requires which of the following in all organisations?
o: A child-rights audit by the NCPCR
x: The Draft National Policy on Child Protection requires a zero-tolerance code of conduct in all organisations.

s: Which Article of the Constitution protects children against exploitation and moral and material abandonment?
x: Article 39(f) guards against exploitation and moral and material abandonment; Article 39(e) protects tender age from abuse.

s: Below what age does the Mines Act, 1952 prohibit employment in mines?
x: The Mines Act, 1952 bars anyone below 18; the Factories Act, 1948 bars children below 14.

s: Which Article directs that the tender age of children is not abused?
x: Article 39(e) covers tender age not being abused; 39(f) covers exploitation and moral and material abandonment.

s: Below what age is every person treated as a child under the National Policy for Children, 2013?
x: NPC 2013 treats everyone below 18 as a child and puts best interests first.

s: Below what age does the Factories Act, 1948 prohibit the employment of a child in a factory?
x: The Factories Act, 1948 bars children below 14 in factories, while the Mines Act, 1952 bars anyone below 18 in mines.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Factories Act, 1948 bars the employment of children below 14 years.
2. The Mines Act, 1952 bars the employment of persons below 16 years in mines.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Factories Act limit is below 14, but the Mines Act limit is below 18, not 16.

s: Who is mainly responsible for enforcing the amended child labour law?
o: Chairperson of the Child Welfare Committee
Principal Magistrate of the Juvenile Justice Board
x: Enforcement powers under the amended framework rest with the District Magistrate.

s: Which policy followed the recommendations associated with the Gurupadswamy Committee?
x: The National Policy on Child Labour followed in 1987.

s: After the 2016 amendment, in which work are children below 14 years barred from employment?
o: All occupations and processes, with specified exceptions
x: Since 2016, children below 14 are banned from all occupations and processes, subject to specified exceptions.

s: The original Child Labour Act, 1986 banned children below 14 from how many occupations and processes?
x: The 1986 Act listed 18 prohibited occupations and 65 prohibited processes for children below 14.

s: To which work does the child-artist exception in the Child Labour Amendment Act, 2016 NOT extend?
x: Child artists may work in audio-visual entertainment if schooling is not affected, but circus is excluded.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about enforcement under the amended child labour law?
o: Imprisonment may range from six months to two years
Offences under the Act are non-cognizable
The fine may range from ₹20,000 to ₹50,000
A Child and Adolescent Labour Rehabilitation Fund is established under the Act
x: The amendment made offences under the Act cognizable, not non-cognizable.

s: Which age group is covered by the 'adolescent' category created by the 2016 child labour amendment?
x: Adolescents are 14–18 and are barred only from hazardous occupations and processes.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Gurupadaswamy Committee?
o: It was associated with the Ministry of Labour.
Its recommendations led to the 1986 Child Labour Act.
It recognised that child labour is tied to poverty.
It recommended regulating hazardous child labour and banning all other forms.
x: The Committee recommended banning hazardous child labour and regulating other forms, the reverse of the statement; that approach led to the 1986 Act.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Child and Adolescent Labour Act, as amended in 2016?
o: It bars children below 14 from all occupations, except family-enterprise help after school
It bars adolescents aged 14–18 from hazardous occupations and processes
It permits children below 14 to work in non-hazardous occupations
It created a separate category of adolescents aged 14–18
x: Children below 14 are barred from all occupations, the only exception being family-enterprise help after school; so they cannot work in non-hazardous occupations.

s: Which law is associated with the abolition of bonded labour?
x: The Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, 1976 outlawed bonded labour.

s: What is the Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act called after the 2016 amendment?
o: Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act
x: The 2016 amendment renamed it the Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act.

s: Under the amended child labour law, what is the imprisonment for employing a child?
x: Offences are cognizable, with 6 months to 2 years and/or a fine of ₹20,000–50,000.

s: Which fund was set up under the 2016 child labour amendment?
o: Child and Adolescent Labour Rehabilitation Fund
x: The 2016 amendment set up the Child and Adolescent Labour Rehabilitation Fund; the Rehabilitation-cum-Welfare Fund came from M.C. Mehta (1996).

s: In which year was the Gurupadaswamy Committee on child labour set up?
x: The Gurupadaswamy Committee (1979) of the Ministry of Labour saw poverty as the root cause and led to the 1986 Act and the 1987 National Policy.

s: After the 2016 amendment to the child labour law, which of the following is NOT among the hazardous occupations and processes barred to adolescents?
o: Hazardous processes under the Factories Act
Helping in a family enterprise after school hours
x: The trimmed hazardous list covers mines, inflammable substances or explosives and Factories Act hazardous processes; family enterprise after school is an exception.

s: How many entries did the list of hazardous occupations and processes have before the 2016 amendment trimmed it?
x: The earlier list had 83 entries; the 2016 amendment trimmed it to mines, inflammable substances or explosives and Factories Act hazardous processes.

s: The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 was drafted by which Ministry of the Government of India?
o: Ministry of Women and Child Development
Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
x: The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 was drafted by the Ministry of Women and Child Development.

s: Under the POCSO Act, 2012, below what age is a person a 'child'?
x: POCSO treats every person below 18 years as a child, in a gender-neutral manner.

s: Which one of the following is inconsistent with the child-friendly procedure prescribed under the POCSO Act?
o: The statement should preferably be recorded by a woman police officer of at least Sub-Inspector rank who is not in uniform.
The child’s statement may be recorded at the child’s residence.
The statement may be recorded at a place chosen by the child.
The child must be questioned at the police station during the night to prevent interference.
x: A child must not be kept at a police station at night. The statement is preferably recorded by a woman police officer of at least Sub-Inspector rank, not in uniform, at the child’s residence or chosen place.

s: Under the POCSO Act, how is an offence by a person in a position of trust treated?
o: an offence applicable only to institutions
x: The Act treats offences committed by a person in a position of trust as aggravated offences.

s: What did the Ordinance of 21 April 2018 relating to the POCSO Act mainly provide for?
o: replacement of mandatory reporting with voluntary reporting
harsher punishment for rape of young girls
lowering the age of a child to 14 years
x: The Ordinance of 21 April 2018 introduced harsher punishment for rape of young girls.

s: Which of the following correctly describes the 2019 amendment to the POCSO Act?
o: It introduced the death penalty for aggravated penetrative assault and prescribed a minimum punishment of 20 years
It removed the punishment of imprisonment for aggravated penetrative assault
It made all POCSO offences compoundable
It reduced the minimum punishment to 7 years
x: The 2019 amendment provided for the death penalty in aggravated penetrative assault cases and prescribed a minimum punishment of 20 years. The POCSO Rules were framed in 2020.

s: Under the POCSO Act, below what age is a person's consent legally irrelevant?
x: POCSO fixes the relevant age at 18 years, so apparent consent below 18 is irrelevant.

s: Which one of the following correctly describes the trial framework under the POCSO Act?
o: Trial before the High Court within one month without compensation provisions
In-camera trial, with investigation targeted within two months and trial within one year
Open trial within two years after investigation by any police station
Trial only before a Juvenile Justice Board within six months
x: POCSO provides for in-camera proceedings, investigation within two months and trial within one year; special courts also address compensation and rehabilitation.

s: Which provisions of the POCSO Act place the burden of proof on the accused?
x: Sections 29–30 raise a presumption against the accused; Section 19 is mandatory reporting and Section 22 is false complaints.

s: On which date did the POCSO Act come into force?
x: POCSO came into force on 14 November 2012; the 2019 amendment set a 10-year minimum for penetrative sexual assault.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the POCSO Act, 2012?
o: It excludes stringent punishment for aggravated penetrative sexual assault.
It includes capital punishment for aggravated penetrative sexual assault.
It provides for child-friendly special courts.
x: POCSO (amended 2019) has stringent punishment, including death, for aggravated penetrative sexual assault; it also has special courts and mandatory reporting.

s: Which of the following is a legal provision of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012?
o: Internal Complaints Committees in workplaces with 10 or more employees
Mandatory crèche facility in establishments with 50 or more employees
x: POCSO makes reporting of child sexual offences mandatory. Maintenance Tribunals belong to the Senior Citizens Act, ICCs to POSH, and crèches to the Maternity Benefit amendment.

s: What is the status of the POCSO Act after the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita replaced the IPC from 1 July 2024?
o: Was subsumed entirely into the BNS
Was merged with the Juvenile Justice Act
Continues as a separate special law
x: The IPC was replaced by the BNS from 1 July 2024, but POCSO continues as a separate special law.

s: Which of the following is NOT an offence specifically identified under the POCSO Act?
o: Child marriage as an independent POCSO offence
x: POCSO identifies penetrative and non-penetrative sexual assault, aggravated forms, sexual harassment and child pornography. Child marriage is not listed as an independent POCSO offence in this classification.

s: Which additional conduct was specifically addressed by the 2019 amendment to the POCSO Act?
o: Failure to attend school up to 14 years
Employing a child in all forms of domestic work
Giving chemicals to hasten sexual maturity
Permitting marriage below the statutory age
x: The 2019 amendment introduced punishment for giving chemicals to a child to hasten sexual maturity.

s: Under the 2019 POCSO amendment, what is the minimum punishment for aggravated penetrative sexual assault?
x: Since 2019 the minimum is 20 years for aggravated and 10 years for penetrative sexual assault.

s: Under Section 19 of the POCSO Act, failure to report an offence is punishable with imprisonment up to how long?
x: Section 19 makes reporting mandatory; failure attracts up to 6 months and/or fine.

s: Which Section of the POCSO Act makes false complaints punishable, except those made in good faith?
x: Section 22 punishes false complaints made to harm someone; Section 19 is on mandatory reporting and Sections 29-30 on presumption.

s: Under the POCSO (Amendment) Act, 2019, what is the minimum punishment for penetrative sexual assault?
x: The 2019 amendment raised the minimum for penetrative sexual assault to 10 years and for aggravated penetrative assault to 20 years.

s: Which body launched the POCSO e-Box in 2016?
o: National Commission for Protection of Child Rights
State Commission for Protection of Child Rights alone
Ministry of Home Affairs’ Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre
x: The POCSO e-Box was launched in 2016 by the NCPCR for online complaints of child sexual abuse.

s: Which system provides a confidential, direct digital reporting window for children and guardians to report online and physical sexual abuse?
x: The POCSO e-Box (NCPCR) lets children and guardians report sexual abuse, online or offline, directly and in confidence.

s: What is the legal age of marriage in India, which should not be confused with the age of consent under POCSO?
o: 18 years for women and 21 years for men
21 years for women and 18 years for men
18 years for women and 18 years for men
16 years for women and 18 years for men
x: The age of consent under POCSO is 18 years. The legal marriage age referred to here is 18 years for women and 21 years for men.

s: In State of U.P. v. Anurudh, the Supreme Court urged consideration of which approach in relation to consensual adolescent relationships?
o: A complete repeal of the Juvenile Justice Act
A blanket exclusion of all minors from POCSO
x: In State of U.P. v. Anurudh, the Supreme Court flagged misuse of POCSO in consensual adolescent relationships and urged a “Romeo-Juliet” clause.

s: Under which Section does the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 retain 18 years as the age of consent?
x: BNS Section 63 retains 18 years as the age of consent.

s: The Supreme Court set aside which High Court's ruling that had excluded consensual adolescent relationships from POCSO?
x: The Supreme Court set aside the Calcutta High Court ruling; it did not itself exclude such relationships from POCSO.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the age of consent under POCSO?
o: The Law Commission (283rd Report, 2023) recommended lowering the age of consent
The Standing Committee on Home Affairs (167th Report, 2012) supported retaining 18 years
The Law Commission warned that lowering the age could make POCSO a 'paper law'
The Supreme Court in January 2026 urged consideration of a Romeo-Juliet clause
x: The 283rd Law Commission Report warned against lowering the age, saying it could make POCSO a 'paper law'.

s: At what age did the Age of Consent Act, 1891 fix the age of consent?
x: The IPC 1860 fixed 10 years, the Age of Consent Act 1891 raised it to 12, the 1925 IPC amendment to 14, and POCSO 2012 to 18.

s: Which body's 283rd Report (2023) warned that lowering the age of consent would make POCSO a 'paper law'?
x: The Law Commission's 283rd Report (2023) opposed lowering the age, calling it a route to a 'paper law'.

s: At what age did the Justice Verma Committee want the age of consent fixed?
x: The Justice Verma Committee wanted 16; POCSO 2012 and CLA 2013 kept 18.

s: To what age did the IPC amendment of 1925 raise the age of consent?
x: The age was 10 under the IPC of 1860, 12 under the 1891 Act, 14 after the 1925 amendment and 18 under POCSO.

s: Which High Court asked the Centre to lower the age of consent to 16, citing early puberty due to social-media exposure?
x: The Madhya Pradesh High Court asked the Centre to consider lowering the consent age to 16 because of earlier puberty linked to social media.

s: Which one of the following is an example of physical child abuse by omission?
o: Using the child for sexual stimulation
x: Medical or nutritional neglect is physical abuse by omission. Beating and burning are examples of physical abuse by commission.

s: Which of the following is NOT an example of emotional or non-physical child abuse?
x: Child prostitution is a form of social abuse. Verbal battering, educational neglect and fostering delinquency are emotional or non-physical forms of abuse.

s: According to the Study on Child Abuse: India 2007, what proportion of children faced physical abuse?
x: The study found that two out of three children faced physical abuse.

s: According to the Study on Child Abuse: India 2007, what share of abusers were known to the child or in a position of trust?
x: The 2007 study found over 50% of abusers known to the child or in trust; 97.1% is the NCRB 2021 figure for offenders.

s: Which one of the following groups consists entirely of forms of social child abuse?
o: Infanticide, child marriage, child prostitution and beggary
Verbal battering, educational neglect and fostering delinquency
Drug abuse, stealing, school dropout and trauma
Beating, burning, medical neglect and nutritional neglect
x: Infanticide, child marriage, child prostitution and beggary are identified as forms of social abuse.

s: Which of the following is a cause of child abuse rather than a consequence?
x: Parental alcoholism is listed as a cause. Loss of self-esteem, trauma and school dropout are consequences.

s: Online child sexual abuse material (CSAM) in India is chiefly dealt with under which law, and which rules require large platforms to detect it automatically?
x: CSAM (over 4.5 lakh cases reported in 2023) is dealt with under the IT Act 2000, and the IT Rules 2021 require large platforms to detect CSAM automatically. The other pairs name child-related laws that are not the stated basis for online CSAM detection.

s: What percentage of child sexual-abuse offenders were reported to be known to the child according to NCRB 2021 data?
x: NCRB 2021 data reported that 97.1% of child sexual-abuse offenders were known to the child.

s: According to NCRB 2023 data, which State had the highest rate of crimes against children?
x: Assam had the highest rate (84.2); Madhya Pradesh had the highest number of cases.

s: According to NCRB 2023 data, which State recorded the highest number of crimes against children?
x: Madhya Pradesh had the most cases, followed by Maharashtra and UP; Assam had the highest rate.

s: According to the Study on Child Abuse: India 2007, what percentage of children reported sexual abuse?
x: 53.22% reported sexual abuse; two out of three faced physical abuse.

s: Reported cases of online child sexual abuse material (CSAM) in India in 2023 exceeded which figure?
x: Over 4.5 lakh CSAM cases were reported in 2023; IT Rules 2021 require large platforms to detect it automatically.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Child and Adolescent Labour Act – Complete prohibition of employment of children below 14
RTE Act – 25% quota in private unaided schools for disadvantaged groups
POCSO Act – Constitution of NCPCR and SCPCRs as statutory bodies
Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act – Constitution of NCPCR and SCPCRs as statutory bodies
x: The NCPCR and SCPCRs were set up under the CPCR Act; POCSO is a gender-neutral law punishing child sexual abuse.

s: The Right to Education Act, 2009 gives effect to which Article of the Constitution?
x: The RTE Act, 2009 puts Article 21A into effect by giving free and compulsory education to children aged 6–14.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the RTE Act?
o: It enforces Article 21A for children aged 6–14.
It came into force on 1 April 2010.
It mandates a 25% quota in private unaided schools for disadvantaged groups.
It mandates a 20% quota in private unaided schools for disadvantaged groups.
x: The RTE Act reserves 25%, not 20%, of seats in private unaided schools for disadvantaged children; it came into force on 1 April 2010.

s:
Assertion (A): The CPCR Act, 2005 constituted the NCPCR and SCPCRs as statutory bodies.
Reason (R): The NCPCR monitors the implementation of the RTE Act and the POCSO Act.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true, but R does not explain A: the Commissions are statutory because an Act of Parliament (CPCR Act, 2005) set them up; monitoring the RTE and POCSO Acts is a function later given to them.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Jaya Jaitly Task Force?
o: It linked its recommendation with lowering MMR and IMR.
It recommended raising women's minimum marriage age from 18 to 20 years.
It recommended raising women's minimum marriage age from 18 to 21 years.
x: The Task Force recommended raising women's minimum marriage age from 18 to 21, not 20, to bring down MMR and IMR.

s: Mission Vatsalya, the umbrella for child protection from 1 April 2022, is run by which Ministry?
o: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
Ministry of Women and Child Development
x: Mission Vatsalya is the Ministry of Women and Child Development's child-protection umbrella, covering CWCs, JJBs and DCPUs.

s:
Arrange the following Acts in chronological order of their passage:
A. Right to Education Act
B. Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act
C. Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act
D. Juvenile Justice Act, 2015
x: The order is the CPCR Act (2005), RTE (2009), POCSO (2012) and the Juvenile Justice Act (2015), so the answer is B, A, C, D.

s: Operation Chinnari-Thalli, launched by the Andhra Pradesh Police in February 2026, primarily targets which of the following?
x: Operation Chinnari-Thalli was launched by the Andhra Pradesh Police in February 2026 to target sexual offences against children.

s: The NCPCR was set up in 2007 under which Act?
o: Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005
x: NCPCR is a statutory body set up in 2007 under the CPCR Act, 2005; it monitors POCSO, JJ and RTE.

s: In what ratio is Mission Vatsalya (2021-22 to 2025-26) funded by the Centre and the States?
x: Mission Vatsalya, with an outlay of ₹10,916 crore, is shared 60:40.

s: What did the Phulrenu Guha Committee deal with?
x: The Phulrenu Guha Committee dealt with the status of women; Verma with crimes against women, Gurupadaswamy with child labour and Jaya Jaitly with marriage age.

s: On whose recommendation were stalking and voyeurism made offences?
x: The J.S. Verma Committee (Home Affairs) widened the definition of rape and added stalking and voyeurism.

s: The Phulrenu Guha Committee is associated with which report?
x: The Phulrenu Guha Committee produced the 'Towards Equality' report (1974). The Verma Committee shaped the 2013 Criminal Law Amendment, and the Gurupadaswamy Committee led to the 1986 Child Labour Act.

s: Which committee–ministry pair is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Gurupadaswamy Committee – Ministry of Women and Child Development
Justice Pam Rajput Committee – Ministry of Women and Child Development
Phulrenu Guha Committee – Ministry of Education and Social Welfare
Justice Deepak Verma Committee – Supreme Court of India / Ministry of Women and Child Development
x: The Gurupadaswamy Committee came under the Ministry of Labour.

s: Which committee, associated with the Supreme Court and the Ministry of Women and Child Development, streamlined adoption processes?
x: The Justice Deepak Verma Committee simplified adoption and oversaw childcare institutions under the JJ framework.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Justice Pam Rajput Committee – 50% reservation for women in local bodies
Justice J.S. Verma Committee – Introduction of stalking and voyeurism offences
Gurupadaswamy Committee – 50% reservation for women in local bodies
Jaya Jaitly Task Force – Raising women's minimum marriage age to 21 years
x: The Gurupadaswamy Committee recommended a dual approach to child labour; 50% reservation was recommended by the Pam Rajput Committee.
